Kind Reminders:
1. Since September 21, 2026, the Chinese government offers three online ways to complete accommodation registration for foreigners who don’t stay overnight in hotels in Beijing: 1. Official website of China National Immigration Administration; 2. China Immigration 12367 APP; 3. China Immigration 12367 WeChat Mini Program or Alipay Mini Program. Foreigners or the host of their accommodation can fill it out. In-person registration at local Public Security Bureau is also available.
2. From 15 November 2026, drones are banned throughout Beijing. Travelers should not bring drones when visiting Beijing. If you do carry one, you might not be allowed onto a plane or train to Beijing. And if you arrive with one, the security can ask you to dispose of it before entry.
Being capital of the People's Republic of China, Beijing is the nation's political, economic, and cultural center. Located in north China, close to the port city of Tianjin and partially surrounded by Hebei Province, it also serves as the most important transportation hub and port of entry.
As one of the six ancient cities in China, Beijing has been the heart and soul of politics throughout its long history and consequently there is an unparalleled wealth of discovery to delight and intrigue travelers as they explore the city's ancient past and exciting modern development. Now it has become one of the most popular travel destinations in the world, with about 140 million Chinese tourists and 4.4 million international visitors in a year.

Beijing Attractions
Beijing, the heart of China, is always the first choice of travelers who are willing to know a time-honored and developed city of China. It has been the political, economic and cultural center of China for over 800 years from the Yuan Dynasty. The numerous royal buildings with long history endow Beijing with incomparable charm, not only the 'Nation's Best' but also the 'World's Best'. On the other hand, as the host city of the 2008 Olympic Games, this oriental ancient city presented her best fashion fascination to the world.
Top Attractions
Forbidden City
The magnificent Forbidden City is the largest and the best-preserved imperial palace complex in the world. It has 9,999 rooms in flourishing period with just a single room short of the number that ancient Chinese belief represents 'Divine Perfection' and surrounded by a moat six meters deep and ten-meter high wall. For five centuries, this palace functioned as the administrative center of the country.
Great Wall in Beijing
The
Great Wall of China
is one of the 'Eight Wonders of the World' and is enlisted in the World Heritage Directory. This immense wall was built to keep out invaders as well as to retain the inhabitants. It spans five provinces from Shanhaiguan Pass in the east to Jiayuguan Pass in the west, looking like a gigantic dragon across deserts, grasslands and mountains. In the downtown area, it is possible to climb
Badaling Great Wall
.
Tiananmen Square
The solemn and respectful Tiananmen Square is the largest central city square in the world, which serves not only the city's symbol but also the whole of China. This immense courtyard is surrounded by a variety of significant edifices such as the
Tiananmen Tower
,
Great Hall of the People
,
Memorial Hall of Chairman Mao
,
Monument to the People's Heroes
and
National Museum
.

Due to religion was always related with the supreme imperial power, it at one time served as the focus of religious life with lots of beautiful temples. The Temple of Heaven, where the Emperors paid homage to the glory of heaven, is the largest group of structures in the country dedicated to rituals. To be opposite, the Altar of Earth was used to worship the God of the Earth. The Great Bell Temple, where the Emperor prayed for rainfall in the Qing Dynasty.

Beijing Dining
Beijing cuisine
learns from many different cuisines, thus, thousands of restaurants with various dining choices are available in the capital city. And the best part is that you can splurge at a fancy restaurant or dine supremely well (any much more cheaply) at any of the smaller family-run operations located all over the city.
What to Eat - Traditional Beijing Food
Although there are various cuisines in Beijing, the must-try food should be the Roast Duck, Imperial Cuisine Food and local street food.
Beijing Roast Duck
It is said that there are two things that you must do when visiting this city: One is to enjoy the roast duck and the other is to take a stroll on the Great Wall. There is simply quite nothing like a perfectly roasted duck with bronzed crispy skin and tender, succulent meat. There are literally dozens of restaurants that serve this famous dish, but perhaps the best known are Quanjude and Bianyifang.
Quanjude Restaurant
Top 10 Peking Duck Restaurants
Top 10 Imperial Cuisine Restaurants
Imperial Cuisine has evolved over time to be enjoyed by all of the country's people, characterized by complex preparation techniques, the freshest ingredients and elaborate presentation including colorful vegetable carvings. It is the foundation of Beijing cuisine. Probably the finest expression of classic imperial cooking is the Tan Jia cuisine served at the Beijing Hotel.

Fancy street food and local snacks are a must in tasting the authentic flavor. These dishes emanate from many different cuisines, but the Chinese Muslim influenceis the most apparent. There are probably 200 varieties of snacks and street food in Beijing. Most of them can be found at the
top 15 snacks restaurants

Vegetarian Restaurants
Like fastfood is for people in a hurry, the increasingly fashionable vegetarian dishes are for vegetarians or persons who love this healthy dining style, but not only for those vegetarians for the religion's sake. Merits and Virtues Vegetarian House is a time honored brand that was first founded in Shanghai. Absolutely, there are more vegetarian restaurants listed on page for references.
Halal Food
Feature food from Chinese ethnic minorities contributes a lot to Beijing's colorful dining culture. Characterized by its fresh yet dense flavor, Muslim Cuisine is also known as Islamic cai and Hui cai, the best dish of which is Whole Sheep Banquet which has won wide praise.
Seafood Restaurants
Seafood is a special dish in east and south part of China. It is well liked around the country with its fresh and special flavor.
Hot Pot Restaurants
You will never be disappointed to look for various kinds of food. For the cold weather, Hot Pot is a good choice to try. It is no wonder that some love to have in summer too. Hot pot is so popular nationwide.
Buffets
Helping oneself in buffets restaurants is a popular and free dining style favored by multitudes of people. Many BBQ restaurants and cafes are of this kind. Here are many excellent cafeterias getting well spoken. For specialty cafeterias, Golden Jafuar, Amazon and Max's Cafeteria are all sound ones.
Fast Food
Apart from KFC, McDonald's and other well-known western fastfood shops, there is no lack of Chinese, Japanese and special flavor (such as curry) fastfood restaurants in this city, some of which are chain shops.
Desserts & Drinks
If tired of big dishes all the time, small restaurants offering desserts, milk tea, ice cream, takeaway coffee, and Chinese tea are comfortable places to spend an afternoon. One can sit and enjoy in the small but delicately decorated shops or buy some drinks and candies by the way while roaming about.

Beijing Transportation
Capital Airport
Beijing is the most important transportation hub in mainland China in air, rail and road transportation: China’s busiest airports are located here; it is the biggest rail hub of the country; many national roads and expressways radiate out here. Its urban area also has well-appointed transport system. However, as a metropolis in a densely populated country, transportation in the city’s urban area is a bit crowded, especially during rush hours (around 08:00 and 18:00). During these time periods, traffic jams are common and may cause significant delays. If possible, avoid taking buses/taxis at this time of a day as it may drain your limited vacation time and take subway as the first choice.
How to Get to Beijing
Air
There are two passenger airports in Beijing: Capital International Airport in the northeast of the city, about 25 kilometers (about 16 miles) from Tiananmen Square and Daxing Airport, about 53 kilometers (33 miles) south of Beijing city center. They both serve domestic and international flights; so double confirm which airport you are going to use, especially when departing from the city. Both the airports can be easily reached by airport shuttle bus, express subway train and taxi. There are also long-distance buses connecting the airports with nearby cities like Langfang and Baoding.

City Bus
Over 2,200 bus routes are running in Beijing, including regular downtown lines, suburban lines, night lines and intercity lines. Dangdang sightseeing buses from Forbidden City go through Beijing Central Axis on UNESCO World Heritage List; tourist buses from transportation hubs like Dongzhimen or Deshengmen run to attractions in suburban areas like Yanqi Lake; direct buses run by Beijing Hub of Tour Dispatch from Qianmen to Badaling and Mutianyu Great Wall are super convenient.

Taxi
& DiDi for Ride-Hailing
About 67,000 taxis are in operation in Beijing with the flag-down rate of CNY13 for the first 3km (2mi). The drivers would charge by meter for downtown travels, and ask for flat rates for long-distance trips.
Considering that hailing an open taxi during rush hours may be a challenge and taxi drivers also take orders online, DiDi, the most popular ride-hailing app in China known as Uber in China, is the first choice for its efficient and cheaper price which supports international numbers and major international credit cards like MasterCard and VISA.
After hailing a car, all the conversation passengers need to do with the drivers is to report the last four digits of the number which they can easily understand even in English, and of course Xie Xie while getting off the car. Passengers can also send messages to the driver which will be automatically translated into Mandarin on drivers’ DiDi app, no language barrier at all. Passengers can download DiDi or attach to its mini program on Alipay, the most useful app in China.
Bicycle
940,000
dockless sharing bikes
run by DiDi Bike, Hello Bike and Meituan Bike are good supplements to the mass transit of Beijing city buses and subways. Internet access and mobile apps are a must to use these dockless bikes and they accept online payment by Apple Pay, Wechat Pay or Alipay.
Rickshaw
Rickshaw is a traditional form of transport. Nowadays, modern rickshaw travel is an excellent way to experience old Beijing culture and Hutongs (alleyways). After paying a negotiated fare, the rickshaw pullers will take you through the narrow lanes. Tourists can find the rickshaws at attractions like
Nanluoguxiang
,
Shichahai
and
Houhai
. The price is CNY100-200 depending on the duration and sometimes the extra service fee is charged. It is recommended to bargain for an exact price before boarding.
Navigation of Beijing Public Transportation
Amap, the international version of Gaode Map, is designed for international travelers which makes navigations easier for foreigners in Beijing. Offering real-time bus and subway information even with which exit to take and walking directions, it is the best public transport route planner which saves time and money. DiDi mini program on Alipay also shows accurate location, surroundings and directions well.
Google Map used by most global tourists is not reliable in China as it has inaccurate location data with no update. Apple Maps does not work in China.
MetroMan is also the choice for metro route planning in Beijing and there are 10 language options. Passengers can download data and use it offline.
Payment for Beijing Public Transportation
Transportation Smart Card & Beijing Pass for Foreign Travelers
There are two types of
Beijing smart transportation card
, Beijing Yikatong Card and Beijing Hutong Card with “China T-Union” that can be used in over 300 cities in China. Users can take their passports and go to the customer service centers of subway stations to apply for a deposit card. To top up the physical card, users can go to the service centers and self-service machines at subway stations.
Beijing Pass priced at CNY 20 is a functional top-up card for foreign travelers in Beijing to use public transportation, buy entrance tickets for up to 30 attractions like Temple of Heaven, Ming Tombs and Summer Palace. It can be purchased on self-service machines at Capital Airport, Daxing Airport, train stations and the service office at Dongzhimen or Xidan. Top-up is available at manual service centers and on machines of all subway stations, or on SilkPass App. Marked with China T-Union like Yikatong, it can also be used in over 300 cities in China.
Beijing Pass cannot be returned and tourists can keep it as a souvenir as physical cards are always designed with distinct China features.
Transportation QR Code on
Alipay
and
WeChat
Pay
Alipay and WeChat, two apps that are widely used in China, provide the best service for daily life, certainly including payment for public transportation. Tourists can easily find Beijing transportation mini programs, get a QR code to take buses and subways by scanning it. Remember to link your credit card to it beforehand for automatic checkoff.
Simply Tap Your MasterCard or VISA to Take Beijing Subway
All subways stations of 17 lines has equipped with gate machines accepting international cards including MasterCard, VISA and UnionPay. Passengers can also buy tickets or day pass with international cards on ticket vendors or at manual service center.
What Transport methods to Choose?
Convenient Subway to Ensure Your Trip
The Beijing subway is always the first choice for tourists as it can reach almost all the famous attractions in Beijing. As a populous metropolis, ground transportation is inevitably congested, so the subway is the best choice to ensure your trip as it is punctual with short intervals and easy to transfer within the stations without navigation. If you have a tight schedule, the subway is the best choice.
Online-hailing Cars for Short Distance
Beijing has a large number of online hailing cars and the price is favorable compared to taxis. If you take big luggage and would like a more comfortable ride or the destination is not far, online hailing cars are very cost-effective; also, it is better for a small group or a family for members can split the fare.
City Bus: Budget for Ground Sceneries but with Language Barrier
City buses are the cheapest and some city buses like no. 5 actually function as sightseeing buses going through the central axis. But overall it is not recommended as the stops are all labeled in Chinese with Pinyin, which can be confusing for foreign tourists so you may get off at the wrong stop. Moreover, sometimes you have to walk to another stop for a transfer.
Ride a Sharing Bike to Finish the Last Mile
Subway + sharing bike often make the best transportation options. When your destination is still a little bit far from a subway exit, there are usually shared bikes at subway exits, unlock one to free up your legs. You can also ride a bike for a leisurely sightseeing tour along Beijing’s Central Axis, or experience local lifestyle by shuttling between hutongs.
Rickshaw for an Authentic Hutong Tour
Rickshaw tours are the best way to experience
hutong culture
. Pretend to be an old Beijing citizen and experience authentic Beijing life on the nostalgic rickshaws.

From September 21, 2026 on, China Government offers more convenient ways to complete accommodation registration when foreigners don’t stay overnight in a hotel in Shanghai: Official website of China National Immigration Administration; China Immigration 12367 APP and China Immigration 12367 WeChat Mini Program or Alipay Mini Program. Foreigners or the host of their accommodation can carry out this procedure. In-person registration at local Public Security Bureau remains valid.
Shanghai, which attracts millions of tourists every year, has consistently ranked at the top of China's most popular tourist cities. This makes a lot of people wonder — why is it so appealing? To begin with, as the most modern international metropolis in China, Shanghai boasts the largest number and tallest skyscrapers, as well as the most magnificent night views. A futuristic world constructed by scientific technology is vividly demonstrated here. While Shanghai is more than just modernization. With streets surrounded by luxuriant plane trees and numerous European-style buildings, it still retains the feeling of old Shanghai from a hundred years ago. It is precisely this blend of modernity and retro, Western and Chinese elements that gives this city its greatest charm.
European-style Buildings along the Bund
Besides, by virtue of Shanghai’s well-developed tourism supporting facilities, you will find everything here including transportation, payment, and accommodation very convenient. Moreover, as the third-largest aviation hub in the world, Shanghai has an extensive network of routes connecting to other parts of the globe, making it the first stop for countless overseas tourists when embarking on their journey to China.
Attractions
The Huangpu River and the Bund are the must-see attractions in Shanghai. Strolling along this river, you will have a strong feeling for the contrast between the modernization and the retro charm of the city. On the east bank stand towering skyscrapers presenting a prosperous urban image, while on the west bank is the Bund with a group of century-old European-style architectures.
Yu Garden, featuring a totally different style from its surroundings, is a hidden gem in the city center. As one of the most representative classical Chinese gardens, it fully showcases the elegance of traditional Chinese architecture. Traveling farther, you will feel the diversity of Shanghai more deeply in Zhujiajiao Ancient Town. Located in the suburbs, it contrasts sharply with the hustle and bustle of the urban area. Here, you can quietly admire the bridges and flowing water and stroll along the cobblestone paths, enjoying the peacefulness of the town. If you are interested in Chinese history and culture, you will be amazed about the comprehensive collection of ancient Chinese art in the Shanghai Museum East.

Transportation
Shanghai is the most comprehensive transportation hub in China. It boasts extensive international and national air routes, as well as rail routes, so whether you fly directly from overseas, make a flight transfer within China, or take the high-speed train from other Chinese cities, you can smoothly reach Shanghai.
Besides, there are various transportation options for you to travel around Shanghai. Just plan your itinerary in advance and decide which mode of transportation to take.
Shanghai Pudong Airport Terminal

How to Get to Shanghai?
Shanghai has two major international airports, Hongqiao and Pudong, with routes connecting to 302 destinations in 53 countries around the world. No matter where you depart from – Asia, Europe, Americas, Africa, Oceania, or from any of China’s major cities – you can get to Shanghai successfully. Additionally, the land transportation in Shanghai is well-connected. If you are going to start from any other Chinese cities, such as Beijing, Xi’an, Chongqing, Guangzhou, etc., just a high-speed rail ticket can send you directly to Shanghai.
How to Get Around in Shanghai?
The public transportation system within Shanghai is both diverse and intelligent. Metro, bus, and ferry all take turns to serve your travel around the city. Among them, metro is the most recommended transportation tool, as it facilitates your journey by avoiding traffic congestion on the roads. Moreover, the subway lines cover most of the popular attractions and commercial zones in the city, which provides tourists with great convenience. However, during off-peak hours or if you want to visit some scenic spots in the suburbs, then taking a taxi is also an optimal choice. It not only enhances the travel comfort but also allows you to directly reach the destination.

Shanghai Weather
&
Best Time to Visit
Shanghai has a subtropical monsoon climate and characterized by four distinct seasons. January to February is the coldest period, with the temperature fluctuating between 3 to 5℃ (37 - 41℉). July to August are the hottest months, with temperatures often rising to 40℃ (104℉); and affected by oceanic climate, shanghai tends to be muggy in summer. Besides, there is rainy season in Shanghai that usually falls in mid-June to early July. Your travel experience would be compromised during this time.
The best times to visit Shanghai are April to May and October to November. During these periods, the weather is balmy, combined with beautiful natural scenery.

Where to Stay in Shanghai?
The most recommended areas to stay in Shanghai are locations near the Bund on the west bank of Huangpu River where a lot of popular attractions gather around. Also, these places feature well-connected transportation networks, providing great convenience for your trip. Furthermore, there are diverse hotels to pick, ranging from mid-range to high-end. Just standing by the hotel window, you can enjoy an enchanting night view of the Bund. However, the accommodation expenses in these areas are relatively high.
If you want to stay in a more cost-effective hotel, then locations near all the subway stations on the west bank of Huangpu River are suitable. Additionally, if you are a business traveler, then living in places on the east bank would be ideal since major conference centers are located here.
How Long to Stay in Shanghai?
Tourists with a tight schedule can generally complete an itinerary in 2 - 3 days by visiting core landmarks such as the Bund, Yu Garden, Lujiazui, and Nanjing Road. If you are interested in Chinese history and culture, it’s recommended to spend an extra day to visit the Shanghai Museum East and explore the Shikumen buildings of Tianzifang. Anyway, it’s not possible to fully explore Shanghai in just one short journey since its diverse landscapes are scattered at every corner of the city. Yet regardless of how much time you spend here, you’ll always gain a precious travel memory.
Shanghai Food
Shanghai Food: Pan-fried Pork Bun
Shanghai local cuisine offers a balanced flavor of sweetness and saltiness. Braised pork is one of the most representative Shanghai dishes. Having been simmered slowly over a long time, the fatty part of the pork has become velvety so it melts in your mouth immediately, while the lean part has become very tender. Other than that, Shanghai local snacks are worth trying, too. Taking a bite of pan-fried pork bun with thin wrapper and crispy bottom, you can taste the delicious meat filling with rich gravy. The butterfly pastry, with a rich butter aroma, has a soft texture and just right sweet flavor.
Above all, Shanghai is a melting pot of cuisines from all over China, meaning you are able to enjoy various authentic dishes of other Chinese cities without stepping out of this city, such as Xi’an Chinese hamburger, Beijing fried sauce noodles, Chongqing hotpot, etc. Also, Shanghai is rich in coffee culture, with the largest number of coffee shops across the country. It would be very nice to enjoy a quiet coffee time while strolling around the city.
Shopping
Apart from visiting popular attractions, shopping is another main purpose for many tourists to come to Shanghai. Numerous large shopping zones gather here enticing shoppers from home and abroad. Nanjing Road, as the top commercial street in China, houses almost all the types of goods you want, including trendy clothing designed by emerging designers, high-end custom-made suits and cheongsams, as well as electronic products like drones and mobile phones. In addition, many tax refund shops are scattered around the city, enabling you to enjoy Instant Tax Refund service in the store after buying the souvenirs.

Nightlife
Shanghai is renowned as the “Everbright City”. The night view of the Bund, together with that of Hong Kong’s Victoria Harbor, is regarded as one of the most beautiful nightscapes in Asia. When the night falls, ripples of the Huangpu River shine brilliantly with tenderness as neon lights illuminate the magnificent architecture of the Bund and the grand buildings on the opposite. Taking a cruise is the best way to enjoy such beautiful view. Just in one hour, you will be able to fully appreciate the panoramic night views of both banks.
Throughout the city, there are numerous commercial streets, restaurants and various bars that remain open until late at night.

Shanghai Attractions
Shanghai, as the most modern international metropolis in China, boasts a wide variety of attractions that are scattered throughout the city. Foremost among them are the views along the Huangpu River, which divides Shanghai into two distinct worlds. The east bank presents a futuristic atmosphere because of numerous uniquely designed skyscrapers reshaping the urban skyline, with the highest one standing at an impressive 632 meters (2,073 feet). While on the west bank exudes a retro and historical charm, for there are rows of century-old European-style architectures along the Bund, retelling the stories of old Shanghai.
Moreover, Shanghai is home to the iconic traditional Chinese garden, Yu Garden; China’s most prosperous commercial street, Nanjing Road; and the most advanced Disneyland over the world, Shanghai Disneyland Park. If you fancy historical treasures, then don't miss the Shanghai Museum East. Wandering around the Zhujiajiao Ancient Town, you can experience the authentic local life and witness Shanghai’s tenderness. In short, there are always different appearances of the city waiting for your exploration.
Top Attractions
The Bund
– Time-honored European Architectural Complex
On the Bund along the west bank of
Huangpu River
, there stand a series of distinct and magnificent classical European-style architectural complexes, attracting millions of tourists every year. Over a century ago, they mushroomed as foreign-funded business and government offices, transforming this area into a bustling "Far East Wall Street". Now, most of them have become fashionable landmarks for high-end brand stores, luxury hotels, art galleries, restaurants, and leisure venues, standing opposite the modern skyscrapers across the river. When the lights ablaze at night, the entire Bund is dressed in a golden brilliant coat and the skyscrapers on the opposite riverbank also shine colorfully; the beautiful scenes on both sides are reflected on the Huangpu River, forming a stunning dazzling picture. At this time, taking a sightseeing boat and enjoying the charm of this night view while feeling the gentle breeze is the most pleasant experience.
Nanjing Road Pedestrian Street
- the No. 1 Commercial Street in China
The Nanjing Road Pedestrian Street, known as "the No.1 Commercial Street in China", is one of the most bustling commercial streets in Shanghai. With the total length of approximately 1.5 kilometers (1,600 yards), it is a paradise for tourists to shop and enjoy delicious food. Strolling through it, you can witness how the contents of this commercial thoroughfare has seamlessly transitioned from international luxury brands to contemporary Chinese fashion, from daily necessities to high-end electronic products, and from century-old Shanghai delicacies to Michelin-starred cuisine. While you are drawn to the various shops, the pleasant tinkling sound will direct your attention to the distinctive sightseeing vehicle – the retro-style trolley. Riding on it, you can leisurely travel through this bustling street that combines both European classical elements and modern artistic atmosphere.
Yu Garden
– Classical Chinese Garden in Shanghai Downtown
Yu Garden stands out among the modern buildings and bustling cityscape in Shanghai downtown. It was built over 450 years ago during the
Ming Dynasty
(1368 - 1644) and is one of the most renowned classical gardens in China. The garden features exquisite pavilions, rockeries, ponds, curved bridges, corridors, embossments, and carvings, showcasing the essence of traditional Chinese garden art. Among them the most interesting treasure is the Exquisite Jade Rock – it has a history of more than one thousand years, with a peculiar shape and dense small holes all over it, creating a mysterious atmosphere. Besides, the garden also preserves a large number of antique furniture and famous calligraphy and paintings as cultural relics from the Ming and
Qing
(1644 - 1911) dynasties.
Shanghai Museum East
– Comprehensive Presentation of Chinese Civilization
Shanghai Museum East has a comprehensive collection of Chinese ancient relics that not only cover all Chinese historical periods, but also feature extensive varieties ranging from bronzes, ceramics, jade, sculptures to calligraphy & paintings. The Great Bronze Cauldron, as one of the must-see artifacts, has mysterious animal patterns outside and eulogistic inscriptions inside, showcasing the superb craftsmanship of bronze forging existed over 3,000 years ago. Looking at the Sky Blue-glazed Plate manufactured more than a thousand years ago, you will be amazed how ancient Chinese managed to create such a smooth porcelain in vivid color without machines. Additionally, there is another branch,
Shanghai Museum on People's Square
, which now has transformed into a hub of world relics where you can admire exquisite antique Chinese furniture, diverse handicrafts from different Chinese ethnic minorities, as well as overseas cultural heritage such as the Olmec Colossal Stone Head and Greenstone Figures from Ancient civilizations of the Americas.
Zhujiajiao Water Town
– Shanghai's Venice
Zhujiajiao Ancient Town, about 1.5 hours’ drive away from Shanghai downtown, was built along the waterways and so is known as "Shanghai's Venice". The town has a history of over 1,700 years and preserves a great many architectural complexes from the Ming and Qing dynasties. Everywhere in the town are small bridges and flowing water, with white walls and black tiles decorating both sides. The whole water town presents a quaint and peaceful landscape of the typical Southern China style, contrasting sharply with the urban hustle and bustle of Shanghai. Tourists here can’t help but slow down and fully appreciate the beautiful scenery. At sunset, taking a traditional rowing boat to cruise and watching the red lanterns on both banks light up one after another would be an extremely enjoyable experience.
Shanghai Disneyland Park
– Fairyland in Reality
Shanghai Disneyland Park, as the first Disneyland in Chinese mainland and the sixth in the world, is the newest and most modern one. Apart from the classic globally shared amusement areas and entertainment facilities such as Pirates of the Caribbean and Seven Dwarfs Mine Train, it has also created a globally exclusive "Zootopia" themed area. The entire park uses high-precision projections and VR interactive technologies to bring the magical world from fairy tales to reality, allowing visitors to immerse themselves in the game scenarios following the main characters in the animated films. Moreover, Shanghai Disneyland Park is filled with Chinese elements, such as the Tai Chi-wielding Donald Duck, Disney characters transformed into the twelve Chinese zodiac signs, and the integration of classic operas of Peking Opera in the musicals, providing you with a unique playing experience different from other Disneyland parks.
Shanghai Tower
– the Tallest Skyscraper in China
Shanghai Tower is situated on the east bank of the Huangpu River in Lujiazui. Standing at a height of 632 meters (2,073 feet), it ranks the tallest building in China and the third tallest in the world. The entire building features a spiral ascending streamline shape. Looking afar, it seems like a giant dragon in silver scales leaping out of the river and hovering beneath the sky. It's fascinating that many people give it the nickname "egg whisk" due to its unique design. Shanghai Tower has a total of 127 floors on the ground. Every year, countless tourists come for a visit, taking the world’s fastest elevator to reach the "Top of Shanghai Observator" on the 118th floor in just about 55 seconds, and then enjoying a 360-degree panoramic view of Shanghai.

Shanghai Dining: What & Where to Eat
As the locals in Shanghai put it, “Blessed are those born in Shanghai as they have the most chances to taste delicious food”. Shanghai is a multicultural city where people from different regions and with different cultural backgrounds gather, bringing their own culinary traditions. Shanghai dining is not one of the
Eight Major Cuisines of China
, but rather a fusion of the most appealing aspects of these other national styles of food. The catering industry in Shanghai is thriving, with a wide variety of restaurants to choose from, providing a rich selection of dishes. Additionally, Shanghai people have high standards for food quality and taste, and enjoy fine-tuned cooking. Therefore, it may be safely said that you can enjoy all the best food from home and abroad for all budgets when in Shanghai. What to eat in Shanghai? The following is the detailed information:
Shanghai Cuisine
Shanghai cuisine, also known as Benbang cuisine, is characterized by its rich sauces and spices, fresh and delicate flavors. No matter what dish, it exudes the refined tone of Shanghai people. Here you can find both the rich and savory flavors of Braised Pork in Brown Sauce (Hong Shao Rou), as well as the refined elegance of Steamed Mixed Shreds of Chicken, Ham and Pork (Kou San Si), all of which embody the essence of a well-rounded cuisine. There are also delicious street foods such as Steamed Stuffed Bun (Xiao Long Bao) and Fried Stuffed Bun (Sheng Jian Bao) to savor at any moment. Shanghai Transportation
Shanghai, as the most modern international metropolis in China, has an all-round development of transportation system. No matter where you are now – overseas or in other parts of China – there are efficient and convenient transportation modes you can choose to reach Shanghai, and the diverse transportation options within the city also contribute to a worry-free Shanghai journey for you.
How to Get to Shanghai?
1. By
Air
– the Most Efficient Way to Arrive Shanghai from Afar
Suppose your first destination in China is Shanghai, taking the plane is the most efficient way. Shanghai airports rank among the top three busiest airports in the world because of their wide coverage of airline service and dense air routes over the globe. At present, there are two airports in Shanghai –
Pudong International Airport
and
Hongqiao International Airport
, with the former being the major international aviation hub whose air routes are available in more than 130 cities overseas, and the latter mainly providing flight service in Chinese mainland mostly, as well as a few short-haul routes to Hong Kong, Macao, Taiwan, Japan, and South Korea.
By virtue of its extensive and convenient air service, Shanghai has constantly been the first stop when a large number of international tourists travel in China, as well as the transfer stop as many tourists travel to other Asian countries such as Japan and South Korea.
Terminal of Shanghai Pudong International Airport
2. By
Bullet Train
– More Efficient Option to Reach Shanghai within a Short-to-Medium Distance
Taking the bullet train can be a good choice if you depart from other Chinese cities to Shanghai, since 97% of Chinese cities have direct high-speed rail connections to Shanghai. In particular, if your departure location is not too far away from Shanghai, taking the high-speed train will be more cost-effective. For instance, it only takes 30 - 60 minutes to arrive Shanghai from its neighboring cities in the Yangtze River Delta including Suzhou, Hangzhou, Nanjing, etc. and 4 - 5 hours from central part of China like Beijing.
Nevertheless, the train journey from farther cities such as Xi'an and Chongqing to Shanghai takes a relatively longer time, approximately 6 hours. Therefore, if you have a tight schedule, you are more recommended to travel by air, which allows you to arrive in 2 - 2.5 hours.
Among all railway stations in the city,
Shanghai Railway Station
is the closest one to Shanghai downtown, followed by
Shanghai South Railway Station
and
Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station
. They all link with metro lines that can reach
the Bund
in 20 - 40 minutes.
Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station

3. By
Cruise
Thanks to its advantageous location along the coast, Shanghai also has a well-developed maritime transportation system. The international cruise routes mainly include Japan, South Korea, and some Southeastern Asian countries such as Singapore and Malaysia and finally arrive at Shanghai Wusongkou International Cruise Terminal.
Shanghai Cruise
Shanghai Cruise on the Sea
How to Get Around in Shanghai?
The transportation within Shanghai is efficient and travelers-friendly as well, with a diverse range of public transportation modes for you to pick. Subway, buses, and taxis all provide real-time service for you to visit various attractions and commercial districts; feature transportation like ferries, sightseeing buses, and the bund sightseeing tunnel are also available, not only facilitating your itinerary but also offering you unique experience to appreciate beautiful views of Shanghai.
1. By
Metro
Taking the metro is preferred for traveling around Shanghai, especially during morning and evening peak hours on weekdays, which helps you in avoiding the traffic congestion on the roads. Besides, taking the subway is very economical, with a one-way fare ranging from CNY 3 to 26.
Currently, there are 20 metro lines in service in Shanghai. They not only connect the two airports and major railway stations, but also cover most attractions and commercial districts. For example, Shanghai Metro
Line 1
links Hongqiao International Airport, Hongqiao Railway Station and the Bund; and
Line 2
passes through Pudong International Airport, Shanghai Railway Station, Shanghai South Railway Station, People's Square, as well as
Shanghai Tower
, etc.
Train Platform of Shanghai Metro Line 2
Inside Shanghai Metro Train

How to Take Shanghai Metro
2. By
Taxi
Shanghai Taxi
If you are burdened with luggage, then taking the taxi would be more comfortable, since taking the subway involves going back and forth between the station halls and the train platforms, as well as going through luggage security checks, which are inevitable. Moreover, traveling by taxi is one of the recommended modes during off-peak hours. Whether hailing a taxi by the roadside or ordering a taxi ride through the online platform, you can quickly board the vehicle and set off. Particularly if you want to visit some scenic spots in the suburbs of Shanghai, such as
Zhujiajiao Water Town
, whose entrance to the scenic area is about 15 minutes' walk from the nearest subway station, taking a taxi can send you directly to the destination.
The taxi fare in Shanghai is relatively reasonable. The cost for traveling between attractions within the city is approximately CNY 40 - 80 (USD 6 - 12), while the fare for going to the airport or more distant suburban attractions is about CNY 150 - 300 (USD 23 - 45).
3. By Bus
There are diverse buses in Shanghai, including City Bus, Sightseeing Bus, Tourist Bus, as well as Long-distance Bus.
City Bus
: The city buses have extensive routes covering almost everywhere around Shanghai, serving as an alternative to the metro and perfectly making up for the inconvenience of some subway stations being a bit far from the entrance of certain tourist attractions. During off-peak hours, you may consider traveling by city bus, which helps you save money and also offer you convenience to admire the street views along the journey.
Sightseeing Bus
: Shanghai boasts a lot of sightseeing buses, allowing you to visit the city’s landmark attractions in one go. What’s more, the buses are equipped with headphones that support multiple languages, making it easier for you to understand the history and fascinating stories behind different attractions. The most recommended sightseeing bus route is City Sightseeing Line 1, which connects the Bund, Lujiazui, Yu Garden, Nanjing Road, and People’s Square, among other core attractions.
Shanghai Sightseeing Bus
Shanghai Tourist Buses
Tourist Bus
: There are many tourist buses heading for scenic areas that are far away from the city center or located in some nearby cities. For instance, you can take the tourist bus from Shanghai South Railway Station directly to
Shanghai Disneyland Park
in 40 minutes at the cost of CNY 10, which is more time-saving and relaxing than taking the crowded metro. Besides, there are tourist buses from Shanghai Hongqiao Airport / Railway Station to
Wuzhen Water Town
operating four times each day, with the one-way ticket fare of CNY 55.
Long-distance Bus
: If you are going to travel from Shanghai downtown to suburbs or its neighboring cities like Suzhou and Hangzhou, there are also long-distance buses for your consideration except for bullet trains.
4. By
Ferry
/
Bund Sightseeing Tunnel
Taking ferry is the most cost-effective way to travel between the banks of the Huangpu River. For just CNY 2, you can get to the opposite bank in 10 minutes. As a bonus, you avoid the overcrowded entries / exits of the metro station, and gain an unforgettable experience to enjoy the fabulous river views. Additionally, if you want to visit
Chongming Island
, Changxing Island, or Hengsha Island near Shanghai downtown, you can also take the ferry.
The Bund Sightseeing Tunnel offers another way to travel between the two sides of the Huangpu River, providing a direct 3- to 5-minute passage to the opposite bank. As you go through the tunnel, you’ll experience fascinating visual and auditory effects that create a sensation of traveling through time and space. However, it’s somewhat more expensive, with a one-way fare of CNY 50.
5. By Shared Bicycle
With pleasant weather, riding a bike to tour around Shanghai is really enjoyable, which helps you save energy and allows you to fully capture the multifarious scenery from place to place. The most recommended cycling route is the Greenway along the east bank of the Huangpu River, where you can take in the river views and landmarks of Shanghai such as the Bund Architectural Complex and the Oriental Pearl Tower.
Shanghai Ferries
Shanghai Shared Bicycles
How to Pay for Public Transportation in Shanghai?
1. Using NFC Payment
If your phone supports NFC payment, you can add your bank card such as UnionPay chip cards, Visa cards, Mastercards, American Express, and JCB contactless cards to the Wallet application such Apple Pay on your phone. Just make sure that there is sufficient balance in your card and that low-value password-free payment works, and then you can pay for metro ride by swiping NFC.
2. By Cash
Cash is the most direct way to pay for public transportation in Shanghai. However, you are advised to prepare some change in advance since payment for the bus fee is usually in a self-help way, CNY 2 per trip. As for buying metro tickets, there are self-service ticket machines in the station halls that accept only banknotes of denominations of CNY 5, 10, and 20. You can also buy the metro ticket at the manual service counter, which is available in every metro station hall.
3. Using
Shanghai Public Transportation Card
Shanghai Metro Three-Day Pass
You can use Shanghai Public Transportation Card in any transportation scenario, including taking the metro and bus, and even the ferry and Shanghai taxi. The card comes in two varieties, one is purple that can only be used in Shanghai, and the other is red that is valid nationwide. Both cost CNY 20 each, and can be purchased in most metro stations.
4. Using Metro Day Pass
One-day Travel Pass and Three-day Travel Pass are two types of metro tickets mostly suitable for travelers. They can be purchased both at self-service ticket machines and the manual service counters in most subway stations.
The One-day Travel Pass costs CNY 18 and can be used unlimited times within 24 hours; the Three-day Travel Pass costs CNY 45 and can be used unlimited times within 72 hours. You may decide which ticket to buy based on your stay in Shanghai.
5. WeChat / Alipay QR Code Scanning
If you have a WeChat or Alipay account with proper payment functionality, you will find it much easier to use any mode of transportation. First, add the ride codes for Shanghai Metro and city buses on the WeChat Ride mini-program or in the Transport section of Alipay. Then, simply open the corresponding ride code before boarding to pay the fare. For taking taxis, you can choose to order one online in the travel service section of the ride application, or scan the driver’s QR code after arriving at your destination for payment.

Guilin Travel Guide
Praised by travelers and poets for nearly a millennium, the timeless saying “East or west, Guilin landscape is best” perfectly encapsulates the city’s unparalleled natural beauty. Winding gently through rolling karst mountains, the clear Li River paints a living three-dimensional landscape, bringing the vision of an earthly paradise to vivid life.
The Li River meanders through jagged karst peaks like a dark green ribbon. At dawn, local fishermen glide on bamboo rafts through wispy morning mist, while lush riverside rice paddies sway softly in the breeze. This timeless pastoral scenery has been immortalized in ancient poems, traditional ink wash paintings and countless photographs, defining the quintessential charm of Chinese landscapes and drawing global travelers to witness its breathtaking beauty in person.
Enjoying the Rural Scenery of Yangshuo
The soul of Guilin lies in the relationship between water and mountains. For millions of years, geological erosion has sculpted limestone landforms into graceful peaks, with sinuous rivers curling around their bases. Every bend of the river unveils a distinct view, ensuring every snapshot taken here turns into a stunning postcard.
Beyond natural wonders, Guilin is home to over ten ethnic minority groups. Travelers can immerse themselves in authentic ethnic cultures through vibrant traditional performances, experience local customs by donning distinctive ethnic costumes, and even join local villagers in field work to taste genuine rural livelihoods.
Guilin is never meant for rushed, whirlwind sightseeing. It is a destination designed for slow, immersive travel. The ideal way to embrace its charm is cycling through rural fields, settling down at a riverside café at dusk, and watching mountain shadows fade gently into the twilight sky.

Best Attractions & Things to Do in Guilin
Unlike cities where major attractions are concentrated in the downtown area, Guilin’s highlights are widely dispersed, mainly spanning three core areas: Guilin urban area, Yangshuo County, and Longji Rice Terraces Scenic Area.
Guilin Urban & Surrounding Areas: The most iconic landmark is Elephant Trunk Hill, whose shape resembling an elephant drinking water has long become a symbol of Guilin. Reed Flute Cave is hailed as a natural museum of karst topography, where illuminated stalactites and stalagmites form whimsical rock formations, granting it the honorable title of “Palace of Natural Art”. Nevertheless, the essence of Guilin’s beauty lies in the meandering Li River. A river cruise departing from Mopanshan Pier in Guilin all the way to Yangshuo delivers an uninterrupted visual feast.
Yangshuo: As the renowned saying goes, “Guilin's landscape is among the finest in China, while Yangshuo’s scenery tops all of Guilin.” Yangshuo features an exquisite, refined pastoral landscape elsewhere. Bamboo rafting on the Yulong River offers a quieter, more serene experience than Li River cruises. The river’s mirror-like surface perfectly reflects towering karst peaks, bringing the poetic verse “a boat gliding on emerald waves, travelers wandering in a painting” to life. More than a scenic spot, Yangshuo is a sanctuary for slow-paced, idyllic rural living.
Longji Rice Terraces Scenic Area: The rice terraces layer upon layer‌ from mountain bases all the way to summits, presenting varied stunning scenery across seasons. In spring, when filled with water, they resemble countless mirrors embedded in the hills; in summer, they become rolling green waves swaying with the wind; and in autumn, as rice ripens, they turn a golden hue. While admiring the layered terraced scenery, visitors can also step into traditional stilted buildings to experience local lifestyles and authentic farming traditions.

Transportation
Guilin is a transportation hub in Guangxi, with many ways to get in and out. However, given the scattered distribution and long distances between core attractions, careful planning of travel routes and transportation modes is essential.
How to Get to Guilin?
Guilin is easily accessible via air and high-speed rail. Guilin Liangjiang International Airport operates direct flights to major Chinese cities, as well as international routes to Malaysia, Vietnam and South Korea. For destinations without direct flights, travelers can fly to Guangzhou or Shenzhen first, then transfer to a high-speed train bound for Guilin. The city has three railway stations, among which Guilin Railway Station sits closest to the downtown core.
Guilin Liangjiang International Airport
Cycling along the Yulong River
How to Get Around in Guilin?
Guilin has no subway service for the moment. Buses, taxis and shared electric scooters constitute the main daily transportation options, with taxis being the most recommended choice for urban travel due to their affordability and convenience.
A Li River cruise from Guilin to Yangshuo stands as the premium travel option, turning the travel itself into a delightful scenic journey rather than a tedious transfer. Within Yangshuo County, renting an electric scooter or bicycle allows travelers to leisurely cruise through countryside roads and soak up roadside vistas. For a visit to Longji Rice Terraces, private car charters or guided group tours are highly recommended. The winding mountain roads require skilled local drivers familiar with the terrain, ensuring a safer and smoother trip.

Guilin Weather
&
Best Time to Visit
Guilin features a subtropical monsoon climate, characterized by abundant rainfall and high humidity. The rainy season spans from April to August, the ideal period to witness the ethereal charm of misty rain-shrouded Guilin. Note that prolonged heavy downpours may muddy river waters and suspend bamboo raft services, so it is advisable to check real-time weather and water level conditions before departure.
The best times to visit Guilin are from April to May and September to November, with mild, pleasant weather. Particularly from late September to mid-October, rainfall diminishes, river waters turn crystal clear with maximum visibility, and the Longji Rice Terraces enter their golden harvest season, presenting Guilin’s most breathtaking seasonal scenery.

What to Eat in Guilin?
Guilin cuisine is defined by its signature sour and spicy flavors. Guilin rice noodles stand as an unmissable local staple favored by residents year-round. The smooth, chewy rice noodles pair exquisitely with richly seasoned broths and diverse fresh toppings, creating a perfect harmony of savory, tangy and spicy flavors that tantalize the palate.
Yangshuo beer fish is another iconic local delicacy. The fish boasts a crispy golden exterior and tender, succulent interior, infused with a unique savory-spicy taste and slight malt aroma from local beer. Its flavorful broth is so appetizing that it perfectly complements multiple bowls of rice. Travelers should also try local street specialty “Suan Ye” - seasonal fresh fruits marinated with chili powder, delivering a refreshing and spicy bite that instantly boosts appetite.

Where to Stay in Guilin?
For a short stay of one to two nights, it's recommended to stay near Zhengyang Pedestrian Street, which is very close to Elephant Trunk Hill. Most travelers choose to stay in central Guilin and take day trips to Yangshuo or Longji Rice Terraces. For those seeking tranquility and immersive rural experiences, boutique homestays along Yangshuo’s Yulong River or on the hillsides of Longji Rice Terraces are ideal choices.
Zhengyang Pedestrian Street
Homestays on the hillsides of Longji Rice Terraces
How Many Days Should I Spend in Guilin?
2 - 3 days: On the first day, explore downtown highlights including Elephant Trunk Hill and Reed Flute Cave. On the second day, take a Li River cruise from Guilin to Yangshuo, followed by a leisurely bike ride along Yulong River and the Ten-Mile Gallery in the afternoon. If your schedule permits an extra one or two days, an overnight stay at Longji Rice Terraces is absolutely worthwhile. Guilin rewards slow travel far more than rushed sightseeing. Slowing down your pace will allow you to stumble upon countless unexpected, stunning vistas beyond pre-planned tourist spots.

Guilin Attractions - Things to Do
Guilin boasts magnificent natural beauty and many precious cultural relics. Every visitor going there will be enchanted by the unique karst landscapes, which are embodied in the verdant hills along the Li River and various caves decorated by colorful lights.
If you want to explore the Guilin top attractions in downtown only, one or two days are enough. The Elephant Trunk Hill, Reed Flute Cave, Seven-Star Park, Silver Cave, and Folded Brocade Hill are the top picks of most travelers.
However, most tourists will extend their trip to Yangshuo by a Li River cruise to fully enjoy the sceneries en route. As the ship sails down the river, you will encounter the most breathtaking part of your Guilin tour at the section from Yangdi Village to Xingping Town.
In addition, it will be a great idea to spend one or two days at the Longji Rice Terraces, a paradise for shutterbugs and ethnic culture lovers.
Top 5 Guilin Attractions
1
Li River
Highlights:
A must see during your Guilin vacation for the fascinating karst landscapes.
As it sparkles in the sunlight, the river meanders through lush mountains like a liquid jade belt.
A Li River Cruise from Guilin to Yangshuo is the best way to take in the sceneries.
The Yellow Cloth Shoal along the Li River is where the background of the CNY20 banknote was taken.
2
Yangshuo
Highlights:
One of the most beautiful towns in China where you can feel the rustic charm of China’s countryside.
Li River presents its glamour to the best in Yangshuo. Take a bamboo raft ride on the river is the most-favored way for visitors to relax.
Cycle along the Ten-Mile Gallery to visit a series of impressive tourist sites including the Big Banyan Tree, Moon Hill, and Assembling Dragon Cave
The West Street with a history of over 1,400 years, aka the Foreigners’ Street, is filled with bars, restaurants, and cafes.
3
Elephant Trunk Hill
Highlights:
A landmark in downtown Guilin and also a highlight of the Li River.
It vividly looks like a giant elephant drinking water from the river, a wonder created by nature.
At moonlit night, the semicircular Water Moon Cave between the elephant’s legs and trunk will form a bright moon together with its reflection on the water, which is very impressive.
On the top of the hill stands the Puxian Pagoda in the shape of a bottle.
4
Reed Flute Cave
Highlights:
One of the most famous karst caves in Guilin and even in China.
Merely 5 km (3 mi) from the city center and can be easily accessed by public transport.
Abundant in stalactites and stalagmites of various shapes, like lions, pagodas, forests and waterfalls.
Walking in the colorful cave makes you feel like you are inside of a fairy crystal palace.
5
Longji Rice Terraces
Highlights:
About 80 km (50 mi) from Guilin.
Vast rice terraces reveal the original rural scenery of Longsheng.
Not only can you view the splendid natural scenes, but also have a glimpse of genuine folk life and culture of the Zhuang and Yao ethnic groups.
The two most popular sites are the Ping’an Zhuang Village Terraced Fields and the Jinkeng Terraced Fields in Dazhai Village.

A Classic Guilin Attractions Visiting Route for Reference
Day 1: Explore Downtown Guilin Attractions
Seven-Star Park (3 hours) → Reed Flute Cave (2 hours) → Elephant Trunk Hill (2 hours) → Two Rivers and Four Lakes Cruise (1.5 hours)
In the Seven-Star Park, you will have a general idea of Guilin and what sceneries await you in the following days. If you love to see the brightly lightened karst caves, it’s nice to pay a visit to the Reed Flute Cave or the Silver Cave. Then move forward to the Elephant Trunk Hill, a highlight in downtown Guilin. After the tour, you can board the Two Rivers and Four Lake night cruise from the nearby Xiangshan Wharf to appreciate the night view of the city.
Day 2: Take a Li River Cruise to Yangshuo
Li River Cruise (4 hours) → West Street (2 hours) → Watch the Performance Impression Sanjie Liu (1 hour)
On the Li River Cruise from Guilin to Yangshuo, you will see various luxuriant mountains. It is time to test your imagination as many mountains are named after their shapes. After arriving at Yangshuo, you can have a rest first and then hang around the West Street. At night, it is highly advised to watch the show Impression Sanjie Liu to immerse yourself in the splendid culture and sceneries in Yangshuo.
Day 3: Half Day Tour in Yangshuo & Back to Guilin
Cycle along the Ten-Mile Gallery (6 hours) → Back to Guilin
Rent a bike and cycle along the Ten-Mile Gallery to enjoy the countryside scenery. If interested, you can also drop by some of the tourist attractions on the way, such as the Totem Ancient Path, Butterfly Spring Park, Big Banyan Tree, Assembling Dragon Cave, and Moon Hill. After the visit, take a bus back to Guilin.
Day 4 & 5: Two Days Tour to Longji Rice Terraces
Ping’an Zhuang Village Terraced Fields (4 hours) → Jinkeng Terraced Fields (4 hours)
Take a bus from Guilin to Longsheng County and then transfer to a local bus to Ping’an Village. Stay overnight there and enjoy the sunrise in the next morning. After the tour, hire a local car to Jinkeng Terraced Fields.

Guilin Dining
Rice Noodles
Guilin's central location in Ling Nan has given it a cuisine that is influenced by the food of Canton, Sichuan, Hunan, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, and Fujian. In recent years, however, Sichuan and Cantonese dishes have become the most popular. The development of tourism, too, has had an effect on eating habits, as local snack foods are enjoyed by tourists from around the world.
Among the more popular of these local snacks are
Guilin rice noodles
(mifen), nun noodles, chestnut glutinous rice dumplings (banli zong), stewed duck with gingko, lotus-leaf duck, and stewed duck with ginger. Some of the specialties of the region are described below.
Stewed duck with gingko is a traditional dish thought to be a remedy for lung problems. Gingko, cubes of duck meat, ham slices, and other ingredients are steamed in braising cups. The result is light but savory soup in which the tender duck meat contrasts pleasantly with the smooth, slightly slimy texture of the gingko.
Lipu taro pork is made up of Lipu taro, pork, this dish preserved bean curd, and various other ingredients. The pork and taro cubes are fried separately and then steamed together, so each piece is golden on the outside and soft and flavorful on the inside. Health benefits of this dish include extinguishing any "fire" (inflammation) in your body and improving your complexion.
Stewed clams and chicken is an award-winning dish of Guilin. A chicken, a pair of clams, preserved longan, and slices of ham are stewed with other ingredients in a covered porcelain pot for two hours. This mellow-flavored dish has many healthful benefits.
Lo Han boiled chicken, as the name implies, is steamed with traditional Chinese herb like Lo Han Kuo, astragalus, and codeonopsis pilosula. This refreshing soup can help to lower blood pressure.
Fried chicken with water chestnut uses local water chestnut, quality chicken, fresh mushrooms, and other special ingredients. This dish is delicious and beautiful as well.
Duck wrapped in lotus leaf is very tasty and healthful. First, the duck is fried to a golden brown. Then cubes of lean pork, bamboo shoot, ham, taro, and mushroom; green beans; and shrimp are stir-fried with seasonings and stuffed into the duck, which is then wrapped with a lotus leaf and steamed. The unique fragrance of the lotus leaf permeates the tender duck meat, making this dish especially delicious.
Steamed pork with rice flour wrapped in lotus leaf is a traditional homemade dish. The pork is boiled and then stir-fried with soybean sauce, dipped into mung bean flour, wrapped in a lotus leaf, and steamed. The dish is rich but not greasy and helps to lower cholesterol.
Fried meat floss with sweet-scented osmanthus is a good appetizer with a glass of wine. The pleasant scent of osmanthus is the highlight of this dish.
Sour fried dried fish. Dried fish is smoked with fruit peels and then dried in the sun. The dried fish is stir-fried with preserved pepper and bamboo shoots and then boiled in Sanhua wine and water. The resulting re-hydrated fish is served with spicy condiments such as garlic sprouts. This dish is a mouthwatering combination of spicy and sour.
Another popular dish is fried pork with pommelo rind. The sweet/tart rind goes well with pork.
In addition, homemade dishes like fried beef with bamboo shoot and steamed, minced pork with water chestnut are also worth tasting.
As a famous condiment,
Guilin chili sauce
is also a highly recommended specialty. It can be added into other dishes like Guilin rice noodles and tender tofu.
Local snacks
Rice noodles, which can be either round or flat, are the most popular local snack of Guilin. The thing that sets one dish apart from another is the soup, which is made of pork, steak, Lo Han Kuo, and various seasonings. Depending on the ingredients used in the soup, rice noodles can be divided into vegetable, three-fresh, original soup, spicy and sour, beef, and horse meat rice noodles. The horse meat rice noodles of Huixian Lou are the most famous.
Other well-known rice-noodle eateries include: Youyi Xuan, located at Jie Fang West Road;
Qin Ji; opposite to the local bus station;
Rong Gui, which has branches all over the city;
Liu Bo Niang, which also has branches all over the city;
Shi Ji on the opposite to Weixiao Tang, Sheng Li West Road;
Shengli at Shengli Lou, Wayao Road; and
Weixiang Guan at Zhongshan Road and Yi Road
Nun noodles are said to have been created by a nun in Yueya Hill. The soup for this noodle dish is boiled with bean sprouts, fresh mushrooms, dried mushrooms, and bamboo shoots until it turns golden. The soup is then poured over the noodles, vegetables, and seasonings. The best place to eat Nun noodles is at Yueya Lou in Qixing Park.
Glutinous rice is widely used. It can be made into ciba (rice paste), tangyuan (rice flour dumplings), nuo mi fan (rice dumplings), and zongzi (glutinous rice dumpling wrapped in a bamboo leaf). The stuffing varies, and may include sweetened bean paste. sesame powder, water chestnut powder, chestnut, lotus seed paste, peanuts, meat, or preserved ham.
Zhutongfan (bamboo-cooked rice) and youcha (oil tea) are two ethnic delicacies that are definitely worth trying.

The chain restaurants are spread throughout the city.

For western food lovers, the following western restaurants are good choices:

This coffee shop is a Western style restaurant opened at the end of 2007. It offers German and Western dishes (like soups & eintopf, salads, baguette, burgers, schnitzel, steaks, pizza), different types of coffee & espresso, cocktails and a special selection of spirits & wines in a cosy and pleasant atmosphere. The price range of the dishes is between CNY10 to CNY50, drinks starting at CNY5.

Guilin Flights
(flight search & ticket booking)
Liangjiang International Airport
Guilin Liangjiang International Airport
(KWL) is about 28 kilometers (about 17.4 miles) from the city center. About 50 airlines connect the city with domestic cities as well as foreign countries such as Japan, Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, etc. In particular, airlines schedule several flights daily to and from major cities in China like Beijing, Chongqing, Guangzhou, Guiyang, Haikou, Hangzhou, Hong Kong, Kunming, Macau, Nanjing, Nanning, Qingdao, Sanya, Shanghai, Shenzhen, Taiyuan, Wuhan, Xian, Zhengzhou, Dalian, Shantou, Chengdu, Lanzhou, Tianjin, Jinan, Wenzhou, Changsha, Fuzhou, and Zhuhai.
The airport shuttle bus line 1 runs between the airport and the Civil Aviation Mansion located at No.18 Shanghai Road and the bus fare is about CNY20. The shuttle bus line 2 runs to Guilin North Bus Station, which is only 1.2 kilometers (0.74 miles) away from Guilin North Railway Station.
Ticket Office: Airport Terminal
Xing'an General Airport
in Rongjiang Town, Xing'an County will be built to operate helicopters to major tourist attractions in Guilin, such as Li River, Longji Rice Terraces and Ziyuan Danxia Landforms.
Train
Guilin Train Schedule
(train search & ticket booking)
The Guilin Railway Station (South Station) and North Railway Station are the two main railroad passenger transport stations in the city. Every day many trains arrive and depart, as the city is a hub of the Hunan-Guangxi Railway and
Guilin - Guangzhou High Speed Railway
. The South Station is located to the south of the city center and is more easily reached than the North Station. The North Railway Station is situated in the northern suburbs of the city and has less convenient links with the city center. If the train you take stops at both of the stations, it's better to get off at the South Station where handy transportation to the surrounding places is available, as well as trains connecting to China's major cities.

Tip: It's not easy to buy sleeper tickets at the Guilin sales office, as the city is a mid-route stop rather than a terminus. Therefore, it's better to buy tickets departing from the city in advance.

How to Travel From Guilin to Yangshuo
How to Travel From Yangshuo to Guilin
Water
There are two main docks for passenger transport service in the city. One is Mopanshan Passenger Transport Dock which is near Mopanshan Mountain, 28 kilometers (about 17 miles) from downtown area. Covering an area of 233,350 square meters (about 0.09 square miles), this dock is designed to look like a beautiful garden and has well-equipped establishments including five waiting halls. In the city center there is no public bus to the dock, so tourists have to spend approximately CNY60 for a taxi to reach this dock.
Cruise Ship on Li River
Another dock is Zhujiang Dock which is 32 kilometers (about 20 miles) southeast of the city center and two kilometers (about 1.2 miles) by waterway from Mopanshan Dock. Covering an area of 48,200 square meters (0.0186 square miles), Zhujiang Dock is 400 meters (about 0.25 miles) long and has nine berths, a big waiting building, and a parking lot. This dock is mainly designed for foreign tourists and is the must-use dock for high officials from both China and foreign countries.
Every year more than 300,000 tourists take the cruise ship from Zhujiang Dock to travel along the Li River. Traveling the Li River to Yangshuo is a journey of about 54 kilometers (about 34 miles). The cruise ships from the berths downtown to Yangshuo usually set off at 9:00 and 10:00, and will take about 4.5 hours to complete the journey. A gentle breeze will caress your face and picture postcard riverside scenery will please your eyes as the beauty unfolds around you. However, remember that in winter the water level is rather low, so the cruise is limited to just 10 kilometers (about 6.2 miles) instead of the normal 82 kilometers (about 51 miles).

Chengdu Travel Guide
Chengdu is renowned as the City of Pandas, with round and chubby pandas being its super star. From adorable pandas in the Chengdu Panda Base, the climbing-panda sculpture hanging on the top of the IFS building, to panda-themed cultural and creative stores all over the streets, elements of pandas can be found in every corner of the city. Wandering around Chengdu is like exploring the World of Pandas.
More than these, the mysterious ancient bronze mask in the Sanxingdui Museum, the magical Sichuan Opera Face-changing performance, and the unique laid-back lifestyle of local people in Chengdu all endow the city with extraordinary charm.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
In addition, Chengdu is the first Asian city listed as the City of Gastronomy by UNESCO, and it attracts foodies all around the world with its wide variety of delicious foods, from pungent and spicy
Chengdu Hot Pot
to deep-fried sweet glutinous rice balls.
Attractions
For most of people travelling to Chengdu, the first thing to do is to view pandas and the best site is the Chengdu Panda Base in close proximity to the downtown area. A total of 260 pandas live here, with the megastar Hua Hua. Her chubby face and slow-paved movements enchant countless tourists. Another good place to see pandas in Chengdu is the Wolong Natural Reserve where you can experience a panda keeper’s day as a volunteer, make food for pandas, and clean their houses.
Chengdu is the birthplace of the mysterious Shu Civilization with a history more than 2,000 years. In the Sanxingdui Museum, the uniquely shaped bronze sacred tree, the highly expressive bronze mask, and the large sun-shaped bronze object are simply the gifts from aliens. Besides, Chengdu was the capital city of the
Kingdom of Shu
in China’s
Three Kingdoms Dynasty
(220 - 280), and if you are curious about hero stories of this period, don’t miss the Wuhou Temple.
Chengdu also boasts World Heritage Sites. The Mount Qingcheng, as a major birthplace of Taoism, is a good place for relaxation and admiring impressive natural scenery and ancient temples. The 2,200-year-old Dujiangyan Irrigation System embodies ancient people’s wisdom and is still in operation. In addition, Chengdu is a wonderful place to take a city walk. If you want to visit the most fashionable and bustling block in Chengdu, don’t miss the
Chunxi Road
, and if you prefer to indulge yourself into the most real street life of the city, just wander around the Wide and Narrow Valley.
Panda Base

How Long to Stay in Chengdu?
For most tourists, it’s suitable to spend 2 to 4 days on a Chengdu tour. Two days is enough for you to visit the Chengdu Panda Base and some top attractions in the downtown area like Wide and Narrow Alley and Chunxi Road. To visit top attractions relatively far away from downtown Chengdu, such as the Dujiangyan Irrigation System, the Mount Qingcheng, and the Sanxingdui Museum, it’s suitable to arrange a day trip.
Where to Stay in Chengdu?
It’s recommended to live in the Chunxi Road area, a popular commercial district featuring a great number of restaurants and fashion stores and also the junction of
Metro Line 2
and
Line 3
. So, it’s convenient to enjoy delicious food and shopping here and get to other attractions. However, the accommodation costs here are relatively high.
Another good choice is to stay in the Yulin Road area in an authentic local atmosphere. After you wake up in your hotel room, you can go to the nearby market and enjoy a typical Chengdu breakfast. Besides, it’s conveniently located and the hotel room prices here are relatively low.
Chunxi Road Commercial District
Attractive Ancient Town in Chengdu
Transportation
Chengdu is an essential transportation hub in the southwest region of China, and it’s quite convenient for international tourists to reach and tour around.
How to Get to Chengdu?
For international tourists, the
Tianfu International Airport
is the main hub to get to Chengdu, and it operates over 70 international air routes, with direct ones from Los Angeles, London, Frankfurt, Rome, Paris, Tokyo, and Seoul... Besides, the airport connects Chengdu with over 200 cities in China, like Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou, from which you can easily get to Chengdu within 3 hours by air.
From other Chinese cities to Chengdu, you can alternatively consider taking a high-speed train to the
Chengdu East Railway Station
, which is closer to the city center than the Tianfu International Airport. Moreover, in terms of short to medium-distance trips, such as those from Chongqing, Xi’an, and Kunming to Chengdu, it’s faster and more economical to take a high-speed rail than a plane.
How to Get Around Chengdu?
The means of transportation in downtown Chengdu are mainly metros, taxis, direct tourist buses, buses, and shared bikes.
To tour around Chengdu conveniently and high-efficiently, it’s suggested to take a metro and it takes you about 1 hour to get to most of the attractions in the downtown area. For a group of 2 to 4 people, especially those traveling with children and the elderly, taxis are the most suitable choice by which you can directly get to the attraction entrance. Taking a direct tourist bus is also worth considering. With no need for a transfer halfway, you can reach the Chengdu Panda Base, the Dujiangyan, the Mount Qingcheng, and the Sanxingdui Museum directly.

Chengdu has a subtropical monsoon climate with four distinct seasons. July and August are the hottest months throughout the year, with the highest temperature often reaching near 40°C (104°F). January is the coldest month, but temperatures usually do not drop below 3°C (37°F).
March to May and September to November are the best times to visit Chengdu, during which the climate is mild and rainfall is relatively low, making it ideal for outdoor sightseeing. In addition, pandas stay longer in the outdoor during these periods, so you’re more likely to see these adorable and active creatures at their enclosures.
Chengdu Food
Chengdu is one of the most popular culinary capitals in China, and anyone visiting the city should enjoy hot pot,
street food
, and
Sichuan Cuisine
here. The Chengdu Hot Pot perfectly balances the numbing and spicy taste and the aromatic flavor. Among all the street snacks, Sweet Water Noodles is the most recommended. The thick noodles are coated with rich sauce, and once you take a bite, you will savor sweet, spicy, and salty tastes successively. Here’s a useful tip for you to find the most authentic Sichuan Cuisine: go to the surrounding areas of residential communities and enter the restaurant with the most local people, and your taste buds will surely be satisfied.
Delicious Chengdu Hot Pot
Famous Sichuan Cuisine: Mapo Tofu
Chengdu Local Life
In recent years, more and more people show an interest in the leisurely and slow-paced lifestyle of people in Chengdu, and the topic of “Becoming a Chengduer” has been increasingly popular across the internet. So, what is actually Chengdu people’s life like, and how to experience Chengdu like a local?
After you wake up late in the morning, you can have breakfast with tofu pudding or noodles with minced pork sauce. Afterwards, take a city walk to the
People’s Park
, and join the elderly playing
Tai Chi
and enjoying square dancing; hot pot is the best option for lunch, and after this, the must-visit place is the teahouse of Chengdu. Sitting on a bamboo chair, you savor the fragrant tea while watching a Sichuan Opera Face-changing or Kung-fu Tea performance, and enjoy relaxing ear cleaning, spending your cozy afternoon. At dusk, it’s time to taste authentic Chengdu snacks in the night market.
The nightlife of locals is also quite enjoyable. By sitting on the riverside music square and listening to the Chengdu-style folk songs, experiencing the enthusiastic atmosphere in live houses and bars, or cruising on the Jinjiang River flowing through Chengdu and admiring illuminated views on both sides, you can always sense the vibrant energy of Chengdu.
