Chengdu Attractions - Things to Do
Chengdu is a city of diverse charms. As the Home of
China Giant Pandas
, it’s the best place to view these endearing treasures in the world. As the birthplace of the ancient Shu Civilization, Chengdu amazes people with the unique cultural relics in the Sanxingdui Museum. Known as the City of Gastronomy, Chengdu boasts numerous hot pot restaurants,
Sichuan Cuisine
restaurants, and snack stalls, and any foodie travelling to the city can enjoy an authentic feast. Besides, Chengdu features a slow pace of life, attracting numerous tourists to enjoy a day of locals, savor a cup of tea, and watch a Sichuan Opera Face-changing performance.
No single tag can fully define Chengdu, and if you want to discover its appeal, why not visit the following attractions to explore this dynamic and laid-back city?
Top 10 Chengdu Attractions
1.
Chengdu Panda Base
Chengdu's Star, Giant Pandas
The first thing to do for people visiting Chengdu is definitely to view giant pandas, and for them, the most convenient and popular spot is the Chengdu Panda Base only 10 kilometers (6 miles) away from the downtown area. The base serves as the habitat of 260 pandas of all ages, from several-month-old panda cubs in pinkish and light grey fur to elderly pandas equivalent to 80-year-old people. In the Chengdu Panda Base, you’re highly suggested to view the celebrity panda Hua Hua who wins affection of tourists with a round and chubby figure and slow-paced movements. Many people travelling to Chengdu just wish to see her face to face.
2.
Sanxingdui Museum
Once you enter the Sanxingdui Museum, it’s as if you step in the territory of the mysterious Shu Civilization with a history of over 2,000 years. You can hardly find any museum in the world that collects as many uniquely shaped cultural relics as this one. The Bronze Standing Figure nearly 3 meters (10 feet) tall is reputed to be the “King of Bronze Statues in the World”. The 4-meter-high (13 feet) Bronze Sacred Tree contains three-layered curved branches on which bronze birds stand and seem to play the role of messengers bridging the gap between the heaven and earth. Don’t forget to view the large bronze mask with protruding eyes and wing-like ears. Rather than being a masterpiece by ancient Shu people living more than 3,000 years ago, it’s more like a “Gift from the Aliens”!
Bronze Head in Sanxingdui Museum
Distinctive Bronze Sun Wheel
3.
Dujiangyan Irrigation System
About 2,200 years ago, to solve flooding problems on the Chengdu Plain, people built the Dujiangyan Irrigation System. At present, this system still functions well, and has been honored as an architectural marvel and listed as a World Heritage by UNESCO. The fish-mouth-shaped dam divides the river into two parts in a 4:6 ratio, draining off the floodwaters and providing irrigation water for the plain. Standing on the Yulei Pavilion, the highest spot of the attraction, you can get a panoramic view of the magnificent Dujiangyan Irrigation System. In the daytime, the emerald-green river rushes forward, while at night, under the illumination of lights, the river is in a stunning blueish-green hue, attracting a large number of people on the bank to admire.
Picturesque View of Dujiangyan Irrigation System
4.
Wide and Narrow Alleys
As a must-visit historical and cultural block in Chengdu, the Wide and Narrow Alleys is composed of the Wide Alley, the Narrow Alley, and the Well Alley. The Wide Alley is the widest and most primitive one among the three alleys. While you’re admiring the 300-year-old traditional residences, don’t forget to browse in the cultural and creative goods stores and buy your favorite panda-themed products. In the Narrow Alley perfectly combining tradition and modernity, whether to have a cup of coffee in a quadrangle dwelling, or enjoy a panda-shaped cake in the western-style building, it’s truly a wonderful travel experience. The 400-meter-long (440 yards) Well Alley is a good place to wander along because it’s constructed with bricks used for the city wall of Chengdu in different periods.
Popular Wide and Narrow Alleys in Chengdu
Panda-themed Store
5.
Wuhou Temple
As a famous historical site in Chengdu, the Wuhou Temple enshrines the virtuous and modest ruler Liu Bei and the brilliant prime minister Zhuge Liang of the
Shu Kingdom
in China’s
Three Kingdoms Period
(228 - 280). The partnership between these two people features tacit understanding and absolute trust, and has become a supreme model in Chinese history. Wandering around the Wuhou Temple dotted with ancient trees and steles, you can admire 28 statues of civil officials and military generals, and also listen to the tour guide telling heroic stories about the period of wars and strategies. Moreover, don’t forget to visit the red wall alley here. The lush bamboo grove sways with the wind, and the red wall are dappled with bamboo shadows.
Famous Wuhou Temple
Solemn Statues in Wuhou Temple
6.
Jinli Ancient Street
Your browser does not support the video tag.
Right next to the Wuhou Temple is the Jinli Ancient Street, a good strolling spot with plenty of tea houses and artifact shops in traditional Chinese architectural styles and lines of food stalls. On the stage of the tea house, as the Sichuan Opera actor sweeps a fan downward over his face, his oil-painting masks switch swiftly and will surprise you over and over again. In the artifact shop, you just need to sit opposite the skilled artisan for about 20 minutes, and he can mold a clay figurine almost exactly like you. In front of the sugar painting stall, you can order a sugar painting in the pattern of your
Chinese Zodiac
and watch the artisan making it little by little. By the way, the Jinli Ancient Street is the most impressive at night when rows and rows of lanterns are lit and all the street is in an antique atmosphere.
7.
Mount Qingcheng
The Mount Qingcheng is also the UNESCO World Heritage in Chengdu. It’s one of the main birthplaces of the Chinese Daoism and composed of the front mount and the back mount. On the front mount, you can view ancient Daoist temples and find the perfect integration of architecture and nature. The Nature Pavilion, constructed with timber piles, bark, and vines, is the best example. By virtue of luxuriant vegetation and fresh air, the back mount is an ideal location for hiking. As you stroll on the walkway built on the pool, chirping of birds and cascading sound of waterfalls will linger in your ears.
Quaint Pavilion of Mount Qingcheng
Taoist Ciyun Pavilion
8.
Wenshu Monastery
Iconic Thousand-Buddha Peace Pagoda
If you want to find a tranquil attraction in bustling downtown Chengdu, the Wenshu Monastery is the top choice. It’s the best-preserved Buddhist temple in the city and also a good place to pray for world peace. In the monastery, a distinctively designed pagoda for about 20 meters (65 feet) high will attract your attention. This iconic building with 1,000 Buddhist statues symbolizes the aspiration for world peace. The towering gingko trees and the ancient Buddhist halls complement each other perfectly, and the burning blessing cradles are neatly arranged. Strolling around this serene monastery, your mind will be greatly relaxed.
9.
Chunxi Road
The Chunxi Road area is one of the most popular commercial districts in Chengdu, and also a top spot for a city walk. The landmark of the Chunxi Road is the huge panda statue on the top of the IFS building, and people are eager to take photos with it. During your walk, why not enjoy the delicious Sichuan Cuisine or
Chengdu Hot Pot
in restaurants along the surrounding alleys?
The Taikoo Li commercial district adjacent to the Chunxi Road is also worth a visit. The buildings here feature grey tiled roofs in a traditional style of Chengdu residences and also modern glass curtain walls, connecting the past and the present. Another must-see view here is the panda animations on the super-large naked-eye 3D screen of the shopping mall. The panda on the screen is quite cute and friendly, and once it extends its paw, it seems to come out of the screen and approach you.
Bustling Chunxi Road
Hot Pot Restaurant in Chengdu
10.
Chengdu People’s Park
Chengdu allures people with its laid-back life style, and the best spot to experience local people’s leisurely life is the Chengdu People’s Park. Here, you can stand around the senior choir group and listen to their highly infectious songs, and sit at the same table with local people and play Mahjong together. In the lakeside tea house, it’s enjoyable to savor fragrant tea and Chengdu snacks, and also closely watch performers making a Kung-fu Tea show.
What’s even more interesting is that you’ll definitely be drawn to the long corridor lined with pink and blue paper sheets on both sides. Actually, this is a special way for local people to find life partners, and many people learn about a person through the information on the paper sheet. This can be regarded as the most distinctive cultural scene in Chengdu.

Chengdu Dining
Chengdu cuisine has three categories, Sichuan Cuisine, Hotpot, and Snack.
Sichuan Cuisine
Ma Po Tofu
Sichuan cuisine has developed over the centuries. Its distinctive flavors entice people throughout China and recently in foreign countries.
Sichuan cuisine is famous for piquancy, but its flavoring is complex as well as hot. Typical dishes include the following:
Ma Po Tofu
(Bean curd with mince and chili oil): one of the most influential flavors of Sichuan cuisine, served in every Sichuan restaurant. Chen Ma Po's Bean Curd Restaurant at No. 197, West Yulong Street serves the most delicious and local one. For hundreds of years, Ma Po's Bean Curd has been popular among people all over China, even throughout the world.
Kung Pao Chicken (Spicy diced chicken with peanuts):
a specialty of Sichuan cuisine, diced chicken, hot pepper and peanuts.
Fish Flavored Shredded Pork: fish-flavored dish in the unique style of Sichuan cuisine. Ingredients include shredded pork, agarics, bamboo shoot and carrot. The delicious dish has no fish but has the flavor of fish.
Kung Pao Chicken
Twice Cooked Spicy Pork Slices: A traditional Sichuan dish. The tasty pork slices are fried crisp without greasiness.
If you want to learn more about Sichuan Cuisine, you can pay a visit to
Sichuan Cuisine Museum
, where you can also learn how to cook a local dish!
Famous Sichuan Restaurants:
Piaoxue Sichuan Cuisine Restaurant: No. 10, Qintai Road
Shizilou: No. 55, Shuanglin Road
Baguo Biyi: No. 20, Fourth Section, Renmin South Road

Hotpot
Sichuan Hotpot
When people think of Chengdu, they immediately think of hotpot. Introduced from Chongqing, Chengdu hotpot has its own style ranging from simple spicy to moderate, three or four kinds of spices, as well as fish head hotpot, medical herbs hotpot, etc.
Huangcheng Laoma
: an old-fashioned hot pot restaurant, regarded as No. 1 among hotpot restaurants in the city. It is situated at No. 20, Qintai Road, Qingyang District, Chengu. A worthy representative of Sichuan culture and diet, Huangcheng Laoma offers hotpot, plus stunning entertainment -- a Changing Face opera performance/shadow play.
Shizilou
: another old-fashioned hotpot restaurant, offers hotpots with half spicy and half light soup. It has several branches in the city, one located at No. 2, Wannianchang Road, Chenghua District.
Tanyutou
: near Qingyang Palace at No. 227, Qingyang Zhengjie, Qingyang District, branches all over the country. Its delicious specialty, fish head, differs from that of others.
Snacks
Hidden in the streets and lanes of the city, snack bars still send out savory flavors.
The most renowned snacks include:
Fu Qi Fei Pian
(Braised Cow Lungs): Actually beef, heart and tongue take the place of lungs. This tasty dish is made with particular condiments using a delicate process.
Specializing in this dish, Jingcheng Yuan Restaurant is located at No. 23, Zongfu Road.
Chuan Chuan Xiang
: also called Ma La Tang, vegetables, sausages, shrimps and anything edible can be threaded onto a bamboo stick and cooked in the hot pot.
Chengdu Chuanchuanxiang
Lai Tang Yuan
(Lai's Glutinous Rice Ball): the nutritious glutinous rice ball made by Lai (Surname of the maker) is soft and sweet.
With more branches than McDonald's, Lai Tang Yuan is easy to find in Chengdu.
Long Chao Shou
(Long Wonton): with thin skin and tender stuffing, the savory snack is popular among locals and tourists. There are several branches in the city:

Chengdu Transportation
The transportation network in Chengdu is very developed. It has one of China’s busiest airports; it is the intersection point of five trunk railway lines; it is connected with thousands of miles of expressways and has dozens of coach stations sending passengers to various destinations. Within the city area, there are subways, city buses, taxis and many other transport conveniences for passengers to choose from.
Air
There are two airports serving passengers in Chengdu:
Shuangliu International Airport
(CTU), in the southwest of the city and about 16 kilometers (10 miles) from the city center; and
Tianfu International Airport
(TFU) around 50 kilometers (31 miles) southeast to the city center. Have in mind which airport you are going to land in or depart from to save trouble.
Frequent one-hour flights are available to Kunming, the capital of Yunnan Province. Flights to Xining, the capital of Qinghai Province, take about one and a half hours, with two-hour flights available to Lhasa, the capital of Tibet. It is convenient to visit the Jiuzhaigou Scenic Spot by air, a 40-minute flight to

Xi'an Travel Guide
Xi'an, located in central-northwest China, records the great changes of the country just like a living history book. Called Chang'an, meaning the everlasting peace, in ancient times, it is one of the birthplaces of the ancient Chinese civilization in the Yellow River Basin area. More than 3,000 years of history, including over 1,100 years as the capital city of ancient China, have endowed Xian with amazing historical heritages and cultural relics, which attract people from all over the world to make their tours.
Read more about:
Xian Facts
;
Where is Xian China
Why is Xi'an so popular among worldwide travelers?
(1) Xi’an is the most famous and influential ancient capital in China.
Xian was the capital of 13 dynasties in ancient China, including Qin (221-207 BC)- the first unified dynasty of China founded by Emperor Qin Shi Huang and Western Han (202 BC-9 AD)- the first flouring and prosperous period in China history. In Tang Dynasty (618-907), Xian was the largest and most prosperous city in the world. All over China, you can hardly find another city with such a significant historical status and with so many historical remains. In 1981, UNESCO listed Xian as a “World Historical City”, on a par with Cairo, Rome, and Athens.
Read more about:
Xian History
(2) Tradition and modernity integrate perfectly in Xi’an.
In Xian, the most attractive part of your tour will be the unrivalled experience to enjoy the present moment as well as touch the history. For example, wearing Hanfu, traditional Chinese clothing, and visiting various historical attractions are just like taking a time machine to travel back to ancient times; standing on the City Wall, you will see the ancient Bell Tower and rows of quaint-style architecture on one side, and find impressive high-rise modern buildings on the other side; strolling in the themed streets of Great Tang All Day Mall, actors in traditional costumes give lively performances and you can interact with them, as if you are really having fun together with historical celebrities.
Wearing Hanfu and Visiting Xi'an
Biang Biang Noodles
(3) Xi’an is a paradise for foodies.
Xian owns a reputation as “the capital of table delicacies”, and its specialties are marked by rich varieties and delicious tastes. Coming to Xian, you can not only feast your eyes on abundant historical and cultural attractions, but also treat yourself to real feasts. It’s not a joke that one gets 3 pounds heavier after visiting Xi’an. Must-tries include Crumbled Flatbread in Mutton Stew, Shaanxi Hamburger, Biang Biang Noodles, and Cold Skin Noodles.

Heading to the east suburb, you can climb Huashan Mountain, one of most dangerous and challenging mountains on the earth.

Travel Planning
To enjoy a good tour in Xi’an, it’s recommended to spend 2 to 4 days here. At least half a day is needed for visiting the Terracotta Warriors and Horses; for the other half of day, it’s suggested to visit the City Wall, the Bell Tower, the Drum Tower, and the Muslim Quarter; at night, go to appreciate one of the amazing shows. The Shaanxi History Museum, the Giant Wild Goose Pagoda, and the Great Tang All Day Mall are quite close to each other, so you can arrange them together in one day. On the 3rd day, the majestic Huashan Mountain is worth a try. If you choose to stay longer, it’s recommend to travel to the west suburb to visit some of the grand and mysterious imperial mausoleums.
As for accommodation, to travel around the city conveniently, it’s suggested to pick a hotel near a metro station, especially near the Bell Tower Station of the Metro Line 2 and Line 6, or near the Giant Wild Goose Pagoda Station of the Metro Line 3. How to Get to & Get Around in Xi’an
Get to Xi’an: The Xi’an Xianyang International Airport is a gateway to Xi’an, and has about 30 international air routes. People in Tokyo, Seoul, Bangkok, Milan, Dubai, Paris, Istanbul, Mosco, London and some other cities can take a direct flight to Xi’an. If there is no direct flight between your city and Xi’an, you can consider transferring in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Hong Kong, and then take a plane or high speed train to Xi’an.

Get Around in Xi’an: This city has a high-efficient transportation system composed of metros, buses, taxies, online-hailing taxies, and shared bicycles. By virtue of high speed and high efficiency, metros are more recommended to take to travel around the city. After landing in Xi’an Xianyang International Airport or getting off the train at Xi’an Railway Station or Xi'an North Railway Station, Line 14, Line 2 and Line 4 are ready to take you to the other parts of the city. What’s more, quite a lot of attractions in Xi’an can be arrived by metro. For instance, you can get to the Bell Tower, Drum Tower and the Muslim Quarter by Line 2 or Line 6, to the City Wall by Line 2 or Line 5, to the Giant Wild Goose Pagoda by Line 3...
You may encounter traffic jams by bus, taxi, or online-hailing taxi, especially during morning and evening rush hours on weekdays. For those who want to view streetscapes in a short-distance journey, shared bicycles are more recommended.

Best Time to Visit
Xi’an experiences a warm temperate semi-humid continental monsoon climate with four seasons. Spring from March to May is pleasantly warm and breezy with a little rainfall, summer from June to August is hot and rainy, autumn from September to November is cool with a certain amount of precipitation, and winter from December to February is cold and dry. In general, spring and autumn with less rain and mild weather are seen as the best times to visit Xi’an, when the weather conditions are suitable for outdoor sightseeing and natural scenery including cherry and magnolia flowers, and autumn leaves are fantastic.

Xi’an at night also possesses considerable charm, and so many interesting activities can be enjoyed. For example, you can admire the illuminated Bell Tower, view a light show and a music fountain show on the north square of the Giant Wild Goose Pagoda, and also watch a band perform under the City Wall gate and take an intelligent boat on the moat to enjoy scenery on both sides. It is also a lot of fun to enjoy excellent stage plays such as the Song of Everlasting Sorrow, the Legend of Camel Bell, and the Great Qin, and also performances like shadow puppet shows and Shaanxi Opera (Qin Qiang). For party-loving owls, cafes, teahouses, and bars on the Defu Lane, and bars near the Xiaonanmen Street are recommended.

Xi'an Attractions - Things to Do
Brilliance of thousand years endows Xi'an with enchanting temperament. The city is one of the birthplaces of the Chinese Civilization, the eastern starting point of the Silk Road, and the capital of 13 dynasties in China’s history. The continuous history has left Xi’an a great many historical sites and cultural relics, among which the Terracotta Army is the most famous. Every year, tens of millions of tourists come to Xi’an to admire this “8th wonder of the world”.
Besides, as a prosperous city in the central-northwest part of China, you can find numerous high-rises in the city. Ancient architecture and modern skyscrapers coexist here, giving a perfect fusion of the past and the present. Last but not least, folk customs and food of Xi’an are full of inclusiveness and diversity. All these attract domestic and international tourists to make their tours to Xi’an.
Top Attractions
Terracotta Army
At the mention of the great number of Xi’an’s attractions, terracotta soldiers and horses always come as the first. After being buried in loess for over 2,200 years, the great archeological excavation of Qin Empire (221-207BC) unfolded a massive underground army of altogether 8,000 life-size pottery soldiers, horses, chariots and weapons arranged in battle formations symbolically, guarding the tomb of Emperor Qin Shi Huang who unified China. The Emperor Qinshihuang’s Mausoleum Site Museum has been built on the site to offer more spots to enrich your Xi'an vacation.
City Wall
The rectangular City Wall surrounds the inner city of Xi’an. Built more than 650 years ago, it is the most complete city wall to survive in China, as well one of the largest ancient military defensive systems in the world. Along the 13.7-kilometer-long (8.5 miles) City Wall, there are 18 gates for people to come in and out of the inner city or ascend the high wall, among which the Yongning Gate in the south is the grandest and commonly chosen by tourists as the entrance to visit the wall. Up on the City Wall, cycling is one of the best things to do, and around Chinese New Year, a grand lantern fair is held, showcasing various lanterns in different shapes, colors and sizes.
Giant Wild Goose Pagoda
Located in the southeast part of the city, this solemn ancient pagoda inside the Da Ci’en Temple was originally built in 652 to store the Buddhist relics and classics taken from India by the hierarch Xuanzang. This square brick pagoda is 7-floor, about 65 meters (213 feet) high, and tapers from bottom to top. The night view of the pagoda is fantastic, and you can watch a light show and a music fountain show on the north square. Adjacent to the pagoda to the south, is the Great Tang All Day Mall, a prosperous Tang style block where performances in traditional style are going on.
Bell Tower
With a history of more than 600 year, the square Bell Tower plays absolutely as the central landmark of the city, from which four avenues stretch towards the east, west, south, and north. While in ancient times, it was used as a time teller. With a gilded pinnacle, a roof covered by dark-green tiles, brick-red columns, and a grey base, the Bell Tower shows a superb integration of colors. It looks more beautiful when illuminated at night.
Shaanxi History Museum
In addition to renowned historical sites and ancient buildings, Xi’an further boasts innumerable cultural relics, and the Shaanxi History Museum is the best place to admire them. There are more than 1,700,000 pieces of exhibits in the museum, spanning from more than one million years ago. Must-sees include a tiger-shaped tally with engravings for mobilizing troops, golden bowls with patterns of mandarin ducks and lotus petals, and a tri-color glazed camel carrying a musical band. Since the museum is so popular that it could be quite crowded, especially in public holidays of China, you’d better make a reservation as early as possible. If you fail to reserve the ticket to the museum, you may consider visiting its branch- Qin Han Museum of Shaanxi History Museum in the northwest of Xi’an downtown.
Huashan Mountain
For those who seek for thrilling and adventurous experiences, Huashan Mountain to the east of Xi’an downtown is unmissable. Listed as one of the most dangerous mountains in China, it is famed for precipitous crags, and also narrow and steep paths. In some sections, one even needs to use hands and feet together to ensure a safe and stable climb. Many visitors choose to climb the mountain at night, so that they can reach the top in time for the stunning sunrise.

More Attractions in Downtown Xi’an
Looking across the entire urban area of Xi’an, you can find that the city’s charm as an ancient capital exudes everywhere. As another must to every Ming city, the Drum Tower stands nearby to the west of the Bell Tower. Time has passed along with the bell at dawn and the drum at dust. Right next to the Drum Tower, the Muslim Quarter is a foodie’s paradise. Some of the snacks and dishes have been popular for hundreds of years. The Great Mosque and the Gao’s Grand Courtyard are also located in this quarter.Many people know the Giant Wild Goose Pagoda, but there is also the Small Wild Goose Pagoda in Xi’an. If you prefer a less crowded tour, it can be a good choice. For calligraphy enthusiasts, the Stele Forest inside the South Gate of the City Wall is a must-go attraction as it collects valuable calligraphic works and steles. Moreover, a city walk along the Shuyuanmen Cultural Street, the Xiangzi Temple, and the Degu Lane to the west of the Stele Forest can be taken to view the quaint and vibrant streetscapes of the city.

Xian Dining
Xi’an Dining, also known as Shaanxi Cuisine or Qin Cuisine, is the representative culinary achievement in northwest China. Because of the abundant use of salt, vinegar, capsicum and garlic, Xi’an dining is in general sour and spicy. On Average, it costs CNY 100-150 per person for a meal in a nice restaurant, CNY 50-80 per person in a middle-level restaurant, and CNY 20-30 for a simple meal at a roadside small restaurant.
Must-eat Food in Xi’an
Crumbled Flatbread in Mutton Stew (Yangrou Paomo)
If you ask a local to recommmend Xi’an food, the first one they recommend most of the time is Crumbled Flatbread in Mutton Stew, which is also known as Yangrou Paomo. It is a soup dish that involves torn wheat flour flat bread, mutton and bean vermicelli. The interesting part is that customers can take participate in making the dish by tearing the flatbread into small pieces and usually, the smaller, the better. If some sugared garlic and thick chili sauce added, the taste of Yangrou Paomo will be more delicious.

Rou Jia Mo & Liangpi & Ice Peak
Rou Jia Mo , Liangpi and Ice Peak, the Xi’an style Coca Cola is a classic meal for locals, which are worth a try for tourists. Rou Jia Mo is a kind of Chinese-style sandwich made of flatbread and chopped stewed meat. Liangpi is a kind of noodle-like cold dish made of wheat or rice flour. It has various seasonings including special red pepper oil, salt, vinegar, mashed garlic cucumber chips, and bean sprouts. Tourists can get this meal in alomost all the food streets and roadside restaurants in Xi’an.

Xi'an Transportation
As one of top travel destinations in China, Xi’an boasts an advanced transportation network, enabling tourists to conveniently and smoothly get to and travel around.
How to Get to Xi’an?
By Air - XIY, the Only Gateway for International Arrivals in Xi’an
About 1-hour-long drive to downtown Xi’an, the
Xi’an Xianyang International Airport
is the only gateway for foreign tourists to arrive in the city by plane. It has flights to 55 cities in 27 countries, with direct ones to London, Paris, Milan, Singapore, Moscow, and Seoul. After you land in Xi’an, a metro, a taxi, and an airport bus can all take you to the downtown area.
If you plan to visit other Chinese cities and then travel to Xi’an, to spend less time in transit, it’s also suitable to take a plane, especially from those relatively far away from the city. For example, it just takes about 2.5 hours from Shanghai, Hangzhou, Guangzhou, or Kunming to Xi’an by air, and the flight from Harbin or Hong Kong to Xi’an takes about 3.5 hours.
Terminal 5 of Xi'an Xianyang International Airport
Tourists Waiting for Security Check

How to Travel from Xi’an Airport to City Center
Xi’an Xianyang International Airport Maps
By High-speed Train - Efficient Way for Visiting Xi’an from Cities within a Short-to-medium Distance
In addition to air transport, taking a high-speed train to the
Xi’an North Railway Station
or the
Xi’an Railway Station
is also efficient, in particular from cities not so far away from Xi’an. For instance, it respectively takes about 3, 4, and 5 from Wuhan / Chengdu, Beijing, and Chongqing to Xi’an by high-speed train. Even though the direct flights from these cities to Xi’an take only about 2 hours, in view of the long distances between airports and city centers and also long check-in time, the high-speed rail is more convenient and time-saving, in comparison.
Which of the two stations should you choose? The answer is the station having a high-speed train coming first, because both of the Xi’an North Railway Station and the Xi’an Railway Station are connected to metro stations, providing you with 30 and 20-minute access to the city center of Xi’an. Much more high-speed trains arrive at the North Station, and the Xi’an Railway Station mainly handles regular train rides. Plus, the latter is closer to the city center and adjacent to the must-visit
Xi’an City Wall
, so that people travelling light can immediately begin their sightseeing after exiting the station.

How to Get Around Xi’an?
Xi’an provides diverse and convenient public transportation options including metros, taxies, buses, and bikes, which allow you to get to
Xi’an attractions
easily and enjoy the sights.
By
Metro
- The Most Recommended Way
Travelling around downtown Xi’an, you’re the most recommended to choose metros as your means of transportation. There are totally 12 metro lines operating in Xi’an, connecting major attractions. For example,
Metro Line 2
links the
Bell Tower
, the
Small Wild Goose Pagoda
, and the Xi’an City Wall;
Metro Line 3
passes by the
Giant Wild Goose Pagoda
, the
Qinglong Temple
...
In addition to the extensive line coverage, the Xi’an Metro is basically not affected by bad weather and features a low risk of delay, ensuring your smooth travel. Besides, the metro fare is relatively low, and a single journey costs CNY 2 to 13.
Xi'an Metro Map
Carriage of Xi'an Metro
By
Taxi
- The Fast and Convenient Point-to-point Way
Typical Green Taxi in Xi'an
For visitors in a family tour with the elderly and children members travelling together, and those in a group of 2 to 4 people, taking a taxi to attractions is undoubtedly the best and most comfortable option. By taxi, you can skip the journey to the bus / metro station, and enjoy door-to-door transportation from the hotel to the attraction, which is fast and convenient.
The taxi fare of Xi’an is in a reasonable range, and it generally costs you CNY 10 to 40 to travel between attractions in downtown Xi’an by taxi. Taking a taxi to the attraction outside downtown Xi’an is also a good idea, and such a drive costs you CNY 100 to 200 to the
Huaqing Pool
or the
Terracotta Army Museum
, and CNY 300 to 500 to the
Huashan Mountain
. By the way, to endure an efficient tour, it’s not suggested to hail a taxi on a rainy day, during morning and evening rush hours, or in the area surrounding the Bell Tower that is prone to congestion.
By
Bus
- The Economical Way
Buses in Xi’an mainly include
city buses
,
direct tourist buses
, and
sightseeing buses
.
Xi’an has a dense city bus network, and you can take a city bus on bustling streets and alleys here and reach scenic spots a little farther from metro stations, such as the
Shaanxi History Museum
and the
Guangren Temple
. Moreover, it would be a wonderful sightseeing experience to take a city bus and pass through the gate of Xi’an City Wall.
City Bus on the Street of Xi'an
To visit attractions around Xi’an, taking a direct tourist bus is a convenient and economical choice. At the station near the Bell Tower or the Giant Wild Goose Pagoda, you can take the direct tourist bus to the Terracotta Army Museum, and the journey costs CNY 30 and takes about 1 hour. Besides, a trip from the Xi’an East Coach Station to the Huashan Mountain by direct tourist bus takes you about 2 hours and costs CNY 40.
Currently, two types of sightseeing buses are put into use in Xi’an. One is the double-decker sightseeing bus, passing by many landmarks of Xi’an, such as the Bell Tower, the Xi’an City Wall, the Giant Wild Goose Pagoda, and the Small Wild Goose Pagoda. It comes every 20 minutes, and the fare is CNY 25. The other type is the
Dang-dang Trolley
in dark green and a retro style. Its route linking the city center with the Qujiang area allows you to enjoy gorgeous night views of Xi’an like the illuminated Bell Tower and Giant Wild Goose Pagoda. Furthermore, if you get off near the
Grand Tang Dynasty Ever Bright City
, you can view the wonderful interactive performances here. The fare is CNY 25 and the entire journey takes about 1 hour.
Double-decker Sightseeing Bus in Xi'an
Xi'an Dang-dang Trolley Sightseeing Bus
By
Bike
- The Flexible and Leisurely Way
Blue, green, and yellow bikes are a common sight on streets of Xi’an, and renting one for a ride is quite worth a try. You can stop at any time to enjoy views you are interested in and explore shops along the way. On the tree-lined bike path, in the bustling alleys, and in the
Xi’an City Wall Park
, you can all enjoy a sightseeing ride and immerse yourself in the dynamic street scenes of the city.
What’s more,
cycling on the Xi’an City Wall
is a unique experience that you can hardly have elsewhere in China. While you’re cycling on this 600-year-old building, you will see a clear contrast between skyscrapers and ancient-style dwellings on both sides.
Neatly Arranged Shared Bikes in Xi'an
Cycling on Xi'an City Wall
How to Pay for Public Transportation in Xi’an?
1. Cash
In Xi’an, the fares for the metros, taxis, and city buses can all be paid in cash. It’s notable that the automatic ticket-vending machines in metro stations only accept coins of CNY 1, and CNY 5 and CNY 10 banknotes. The bus fare is CNY 2 per trip and the fare box accepts exact change only.
2.
Chang’an Pass Card
The Chang’an Pass Card can be used for taking both Xi’an metros and city buses, and you can buy it for CNY 13 either at the service center or at the self-service ticket-vending machine of the metro station. This card offers a 50% discount on bus fares and a 90% discount on metro fares. Furthermore, this card has a China T-Union logo indicating that in over 300 cities in China, you can use this card to pay your public transportation fares.
Chang'an Pass Card
Single Journey Ticket for Xi'an Metro
3. Xi’an Metro Day Pass
Xi’an metros offer one-day and three-day passes, which can be purchased at the service center or the self-service ticket-vending machine of the metro station. These two kinds of passes respectively cost CNY 15 and 40, with periods of validity of 24 and 72 hours during which numbers of rides are unlimited.
4. WeChat / Alipay Transit QR Code
You can add the Chang’an Pass QR Code to Cards & Offers of WeChat or Transport of Alipay, and scan it to ride a city bus. To take a metro, you need to add the Xi’an Metro QR Code.
5. NFC
After adding the Chang’an Pass - China T-Union Card to your mobile wallet, you can use the NFC function of your mobile phone and swipe it for fare payment at metro stations and on city buses.

Hangzhou Travel Guide
Hangzhou, located in the southern part of China’s Yangtze River Delta, has long earned its fame as the “Heaven on Earth” by virtue of its stunning natural scenery. In this paradise lies the core masterpiece West Lake where vast waters are embraced by lush green mountains and dotted with exquisitely crafted pavilions and towers. Gliding gently on a sightseeing boat, you seamlessly become part of this breathtaking natural landscape. Nestled among the hills near the lake are another unique sight - vast terraced Longjing Tea Plantations, neatly arranged and dotted with tea-picking farmers wearing conical hats. You can also join in this activity of picking fresh tea leaves, and later savor the refreshing taste of authentic Longjing tea.
Sightseeing Boat on West Lake
Tourist Taking Photos by West Lake
Your browser does not support the video tag.
As a city with a history of over 2,000 years of establishment, Hangzhou boasts rich cultural heritage in addition to picturesque landscapes. The Archaeological Ruins of Liangzhu City, which dates back 5, 000 years, was excavated right here, and the subsequent discoveries of pottery, jade artifacts, as well as palace walls, tombs, and other clues gradually unveiled the mystery of the origin of China’s 5,000-year-old civilization. Another famous historical site the Lingyin Temple that has endured through thousands of years, is grand in scale and features solemn Buddhist architecture. The story of the eminent monk Ji Gong helping people and spreading compassion to all beings has been passed down for hundreds of years.
Nowadays, Hangzhou is even known as the “Silicon Valley of China”, being the top city in China for the development of artificial intelligence. Therefore, in Hangzhou, you can see the most advanced technological products such as robots and drones, as well as the most intelligent urban facilities.
Attractions
West Lake enjoys the greatest reputation in Hangzhou for there is a household touching and heart-wrenching love story of a human and a snake fairy that has been passed down for generations, and its natural beauty has also been vividly depicted in the poems and paintings of many ancient Chinese literati. The 638-hectare (1,576-acre) lake surface is like a huge copper mirror, dotted with small islands and ancient towers, and surrounded by lush mountains. You can ride a bicycle to tour around the lake, or take a boat to slowly enjoy the lake scenery. Strolling further to the Longjing Village on the southwest side of the lake, you can see the layered emerald green tea plantations stretching along the mountain slopes. Bathed in the fragrance of tea, you may already be eager to experience the fun of picking tea with the villagers.
The Lingyin Temple, with a history of over 1,700 years, is another hidden gem nestled among the green mountains and clear waters of Hangzhou. The solemn Buddhist halls and towering ancient trees are in harmony, and the surrounding hills have an incredibly magnificent structure. The wisps of incense float in the midst of the melodious bell sounds, making you forget the worldly hustle and bustle. The worship activities here have been flourishing for thousands of years, carrying the aspirations of countless people for peace, health, and success in their studies and careers.

Alibaba Headquarters
If you are interested in science & technology, you might want to visit Alibaba’s headquarters. This building of China’s leading internet enterprise has witnessed the evolution of Chinese technology time and again. You can immerse yourself in experiencing the future life scenarios created by artificial intelligence, interact closely with robots, or even practice AI technology under the guidance of the guide.
Transportation
Hangzhou is a major aviation and high-speed rail hub in China. Whether you are departing from overseas or transferring from other Chinese cities, you can arrive efficiently. However, since many scenic areas are very extensive and specific scenic spots are scattered, it is best to combine different modes of transportation for your tour.
How to Get to Hangzhou?
Currently, Hangzhou Xiaoshan International Airport is the main airport of this city. It has direct international routes to 53 destinations including Tokyo, Seoul, Paris, Frankfurt, New York, Los Angeles, etc., as well as 127 domestic routes to other Chinese cities such as Beijing, Xi’an, Chongqing, and Guangzhou. Taking the bullet train is another convenient way to Hangzhou, especially if you travel from Shanghai, which only takes 45 - 60 minutes. If your first stop after arriving in Hangzhou is to visit the West Lake, it is recommended that you buy the ticket at Hangzhou Station. After getting off the train, you can reach the destination within just 10-minute drive.
How to Get Around in Hangzhou?
There are a total of 12 metro lines in Hangzhou, covering most attractions in the city. Nevertheless, considering the certain distance between the subway stations and the entrance of some scenic spots due to extensiveness of the scenic areas, you are recommended to take the subway to the nearest station of the tourist attractions first, and then take a bus or take a taxi to the specific scenic spot you want to visit. By the way, cycling around the large West Lake is also highly recommended, which saves energy and allows you to enjoy the lake views while touching the gentle breeze.
What’s more, the unique water bus service in Hangzhou is also worth experiencing. For just CNY 3, you can board the bus and enjoy the city views along the canal as you travel.

How Long to Stay in Hangzhou?
A 1 - 2-day stay in Hangzhou is most suitable, as it’s long enough to visit the main attractions in the city, such as the West Lake, Lingyin Temple and Longjing Village. After dark, you can watch the stage performance at the West Lake, which features a floating and elevating platform where performers dance on the water, with the landscape of the lake as the backdrop. Combined with the effects of lights and holographic projections, it creates a dreamlike atmosphere.
If you don’t have a tight schedule, you can visit the core attractions in the first two days, and then arrange one extra day to visit the Archaeological Ruins of Liangzhu City, admiring the ancient cityscape from 5,000 years ago and the unearthed historical relics such as jade and pottery.
The Best Area to Stay in Hangzhou
The best area to stay in Hangzhou is around the West Lake thanks to the convenient transportation nearby, fabulous scenery, as well as comprehensive entertainment facilities. However, the accommodation expenses are relatively high, especially during the peak tourist season. If you are a budget traveler, you can choose to live at the Xiaohe Straight Street near the Grand Canal where there is more peaceful, flanked by retro Chinese-style buildings, including many nice folk houses.

Hangzhou Weather
&
Best Time to Visit
Hangzhou has a subtropical monsoon climate, with distinct four seasons and humid air. January is the coldest month, with the lowest temperature dropping to -4℃ (25℉). Hot weather lasts from late June to early September, with July and August being the hottest months when temperatures often exceed 35℃ (95℉).
Spring and autumn are the best times to visit Hangzhou, during which the weather is pleasant and the scenery is at its most beautiful. Especially in spring, you can see the Su Causeway of West Lake with peach blossoms in full bloom and experience the joy of tea picking. Although July - August is hot, it is also the peak flowering period of the lotus flowers in the West Lake, which will surely offer you a visual feast.

Hangzhou Food
The cooking style of Hangzhou cuisine emphasizes maintaining the original flavor, with a light, fresh and tender taste. The most recommended specialty dish is Fried Shrimps with Longjing Tea, which is elegantly presented on a plate. The shrimps are crisp and delicious, with a refreshing aroma of Longjing Tea. Next is Dongpo Pork – a delicacy named after an ancient Chinese poet. Made by slow-cooking marbled pork with condiments like scallions, ginger, cooking wine, and rock sugar until the sauce thickens, it turns out tender, fragrant, rich without being too greasy.
Speaking of Longjing tea, it is a symbol of Hangzhou and ranks first among China’s top ten famous teas. It was once the exclusive tribute tea for the ancient imperial court. The Longjing Tea plants are nurtured by the soil and moisture of West Lake, contributing to refreshingly sweet and smooth texture of the brewed tea leaves, with a lingering aftertaste. Guess you wouldn’t resist a cup of it to cool off and relive fatigue while enjoying the scenery by the lake in summer!

Hangzhou Attractions
Speaking of tourist attractions in Hangzhou, West Lake has always been the top one attracting travelers from home and abroad. It’s charming distinctively throughout the four seasons. By virtue of picturesque views, it is honored as the “Heaven on Earth”. Riding a sightseeing boat slowly to the center of the lake, you’re able to fully take in the harmonious landscape adorned with antique towers and pavilions, as well as chirping birds skimming across the water. Precisely such superior natural environment nurtured the most famous tea of Hangzhou, Longjing Tea. The lush terraced tea plantations on the hills along the lake shore exude the fragrance of tea leaves, and scattering tea pickers also become an integral part of this anime-like scene. Besides, in the city stands nearly 1,700-year-old Lingyin Temple where solemn Buddha statues in the main hall and the rising smoke from incense carry the aspirations of generations for a promising life.
West Lake at Sunset
Tourists in Xixi National Wetland Park
Nowadays, Hangzhou, leveraging its advantages in the technology industry, has transformed from a traditional tourist city into one of the destinations for “technology tourism” in which you can see robots making coffee, delivering packages, and even practicing Tai Chi with humans. Moreover, there are diverse advanced technological products you can experience, such as AR smart swimming goggles that can displays real-time data underwater, AI audio recording cards that can quickly converts meeting content into text, and DNA data storage “time capsules” that can preserve precious memories, etc.
You may combine stunning natural sightseeing with futuristic technology appreciation to enjoy two completely different travel experiences.
Top Tourist Attractions in Hangzhou
West Lake
The west lake covers an area of 638 hectares (1,579 acres) and is a must-visit attraction as the symbol of Hangzhou. The most remarkable feature here is the Top Ten Scenes of West Lake, including the Su Causeway where willows sway gently and peach flowers are in full bloom, large area of lotus flowers exuding aroma in the summer breeze around the gardens, and the painting of Leifeng Pagoda and the golden waves on the water at sunset, etc. These views, had inspired countless literati from ancient times to present to compose magnificent poems and paintings. In addition, there is a heart-wrenching love story between a white snake fairy and a human being, which adds some romantic elements to the beauty of the West Lake.
You can take a sightseeing boat to admire the expansive lake views, or go cycling around the lake to enjoy West Lake’s charm from different perspectives. At dusk, the landscape of West Lake turns into a large stage background featuring classic Southern Chinese style, where performers dance elegantly, creating a visual feast exclusive to Hangzhou for tourists.
Sightseeing Boat on West Lake
Lingyin Temple
(Temple of Soul’s Retreat)
Lingyin Temple, as the most renowned Buddha temple in Hangzhou, was constructed during
Eastern Jin
(317 - 420 AD) about 1,700 years ago. Every year, a large number of tourists come visiting and pray before the magnificent and solemn Buddha statues, hoping for blessings such as good health and prosperous future.
The Temple faces the Peak Flown from Afar, which is a limestone mountain with typical karst topographic features. Legend has it that an Indian monk came here on a journey and, impressed by this unique landscape, believed this mountain to have flown here from his home country. Thus, he named it Peak Flown from Afar, and settled here, presiding over the construction of the temple, which is now known as Lingyin Temple, meaning “Temple of Soul’s Retreat”. The mountain is crisscrossed with strange rocks and ancient trees tower above. Moreover, there are hundreds of Buddha statues on the mountain walls, with exquisite and lifelike carvings, being one of the largest and most concentrated groups of cave statues in southern China.
Tourists Praying in Lingyin Temple
Buddha Statue of Peak Flown from Afar
Meijiawu Tea Plantation
Meijiawu is a small village tucked away in the lush mountains on the west side of West Lake. It is the main production area of Longjing Tea, one of the top ten famous teas in China, with the history of tea cultivation of over 600 years. The terraces of the tea plantation here are just like green waves stretching along the mountain slope, with white-walled and black-tiled cottages scattered around and the aroma of tea filling the air, as if you have accidentally entered a retreat away from the secular world.
From late March to mid-April every year is the tea-picking season when the terraces are dotted with tea pickers wearing straw hats. In the early morning, you can follow them to experience the joy of picking tea leaves, and then return to the folk house, watching the masters’ skills of frying tea. When the afternoon drowsiness sets in, a cup of brewed Longjing Tea will refresh your mind.
Tea Pickers Wearing Straw Hats
Tourists Watching Tea Frying
Alibaba Global Headquarters
Alibaba, as the leading internet enterprise of China and the globally renowned e-commerce giant developing from a small start-up company in 1999, has gone through technological innovations time and again. In Xixi Park Hangzhou lies the Alibaba Global Headquarters, which is equipped with smart office operating systems in all scenarios, and is also the birth place of various artificial intelligence technologies. Here, you can witness diversified black technology products, such as ingenious robots capable of efficiently conducting logistics sorting and distribution, intelligent household machines, self-driving automobiles, etc. What’s more, you can immerse in the considerate service supported by AI. For example, there is AI-driven unmanned Hotel for customers to stay, with all procedures handled by AI, proving a convenient living experience.
Six Harmonies Pagoda
Six Harmonies Pagoda
Six Harmonies Pagoda is a historic tower approximately 60 meters (200 feet) tall. The term “Six Harmonies” in its name symbolizes the six harmonious ways of living advocated by Buddhism in terms of words, actions, spiritual thoughts, and governance. The exterior of the pagoda is made of wood, while the interior is constructed of brick and stone. What’s even more interesting is that although it appears to have 13 floors from the outside, in reality it only has 7 floors inside, with the other six floors enclosed and hidden inside the tower, serving to reinforce its structure.
Although Six Harmonies Pagoda was built in
Northern Song
(960 - 1127 AD) more than 1,000 years ago, there are still well-preserved ancient inscriptions by the emperors on the plaques for each floor, as well as stone-carved Buddhist scriptures from centuries ago, which expound on the theories of Buddhist practice. This pagoda was once used as a military garrison in ancient times, but now it has become an excellent viewing platform. After reaching the top, you can overlook the surging Qiantang River and admire the beautiful scenery of West Lake in the distance.
Xixi National Wetland Park
About 5 kilometers (3 miles) away from the West Lake lies a scenic spot praised as the Green Lungs of Hangzhou, Xixi National Wetland Park. The whole park has a water coverage of 70% and boasts superior ecological environment and diversified creatures. Over approximately 800 years ago, this park belonged to royal hunting field, which, with time passing by, transformed to royal garden and private garden in sequence. Therefore, up to now, you can still witness abundant historical and cultural sites, including ancient official’s family temples, time-honored village houses, and vivid stone carvings.
Taking a boat is the best way to tour around the park, which allows you to explore deep into the heart of the wetland and navigate through the crisscrossing waterways, experiencing the tranquility and harmony of nature. Delightfully, there are many bird-viewing platforms on which you can enjoy spectacular scene of large flocks of birds playing on the water or flying to the sky.
Antique Pavilion in Xixi National Wetland Park
River & Bridge in Xixi National Wetland Park
Wuzhen Water Town
Wuzhen Water Town has a long history and picturesque landscape and is about 1.5 - 2 hours’ drive away from Hangzhou downtown. The residence buildings here, all characterized by white walls and black tiles, are neatly arranged along the banks of rivers. Bridges can be seen everywhere, connecting districts on the two sides. Sitting in a black-awning boat to appreciate the water town would be rather enjoyable.
The meandering waterways divide the town into four areas on east, west, north, south directions. Among them, the east area features more authentic elements, possessing a lot of historic structures like temples and opera stages. Besides, you can see many exquisite wooden carvings, as well as experiencing traditional crafts like tie-dye and by the way make a tie-dye shirt by yourself. While the west area is more commercial and has beautiful night views. As the lanterns light up at dusk, the ripples of the river shine goldenly, full of romantic vibes. North and south areas are mainly life spaces of locals, which, though equipped with less comprehensive tourist facilities, are filled with a strong sense of life.
Streetscape of Wuzhen Water Town
Tourists Strolling in the Alley of Wuzhen Water Town
Archaeological Ruins of Liangzhu City
The Archaeological Ruins of Liangzhu City were excavated in the 1930s. The mysteries of the Liangzhu Culture, which had existed for over 5,000 years, were thus unveiled, further confirming the long history of China’s civilization spanning over 5,000 years.
Now tourists can see many historic sites like nobility’s tombs and duplicated manual workshops at the time. Besides, there is a museum in which a large number of ancient artifacts used by nobility from Liangzhu Times are exhibited, ranging from pottery, jade, and lacquerware. These masterpieces, though made in prehistoric period, were exquisitely crafted, with various mysterious yet aesthetic patterns. Moreover, the scenic area is vast and boasts mesmerizing natural views aside from historical ones, where you can see many adorable sika deer and have a relaxing hike.

Restaurants of Hangzhou Cuisine
There are several dishes that have come down over several hundred years, some even thousands of years. They are West Lake Fish in Vinegar Gravy, Braised Dong Po Pork, Beggar's Chicken and Fried Shrimps with Long Jing Tea Leaves. These dishes are pleasant from their color, smell and taste. It is also a good choice to walk around these snack streets to experience the local culture.

Hangzhou, the capital city of Zhejiang Province, is one of the top choices for people who would like to enjoy a side trip after touring Shanghai. Travelers at home and abroad are attracted by its fascinating

Xiaoshan International Airport
Xiaoshan International Airport
(HGH), around 17mi (27km) from the downtown, mainly serves Hangzhou and nearby cities like Huzhou, Shaoxing, Jiaxing, and Zhuji. It operates many air routes with Terminal A (International) and Terminal B (Domestic). Besides Hong Kong, Macau and Taipei, the international destinations include Singapore, Souel, Amsterdam, Pattaya, Phuket Island, Osaka, Tokyo, and Chiengmai. Domestic air routes from/to Beijing, Chengdu, Jiuzhaigou, Guangzhou, Guilin, Xian, Kunming, Lhasa, and Xiamen are available.

Hangzhou Railway Station

East Railway Station
: It lies on Tiancheng Road, Jianggan District. Opened in 2013, it is now one of the largest high speed train hubs in east China, transporting a large amount of passengers daily.

: Originally named Xiaoshan Railway Station, it is around 17mi (27km) from Chengzhan Railway Station. The station hosts trains passing through the city. Now it is closed for renovation since Jul. 2013 and is expected to reopen in late 2019.

Chongqing Travel Guide
In recent years, Chongqing has risen to worldwide online fame with iconic monikers including the “Cyberpunk” and “8D Magic City”. Light rail trains gliding through residential buildings, the mesmerizing night scenery of Hongya Cave reminiscent of scenes from Hayao Miyazaki’s animated classic Spirited Away, and its intricate layered network of overpasses and pedestrian walkways endow the city with a striking futuristic and sci-fi aesthetic. Beneath these surreal urban landscapes lies Chongqing’s distinctive rugged topography. Nestled amid rolling hills at the confluence of the Yangtze and Jialing Rivers, the city features steep slopes, towering cliffs and winding waterways, crafting a one-of-a-kind three-dimensional urban landscape with dramatic elevation variations.
Yangtze River Cruise
Boasting a time-honored and profound cultural heritage, Chongqing preserves countless historical tales within its ancient stone staircases and old alleyways. Its history stretches back to the ancient Ba Kingdom (1122 BC - 316 BC), followed by its official naming as “Chongqing” in the
Southern Song Dynasty
(1127 - 1279), and it later served as the wartime capital during the Chinese People’s War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression.
As the pivotal departure point for Yangtze River cruises, Chongqing’s
Chaotianmen Dock
welcomes travelers from across the globe, who embark on downstream voyages to explore the breathtaking gorges. Today, this former industrial hub has embraced remarkable modern transformation, where sleek contemporary skyscrapers stand in perfect harmony with traditional stilted dwellings, cementing its status as one of China’s most coveted travel destinations.
You may like:
Top 10 Things to Do in Chongqing
Attractions
Your browser does not support the video tag.
Mirroring its diverse terrain, Chongqing’s tourist attractions feature unique layering and striking contrasts. Hongya Cave stands as an unmissable landmark, a sprawling complex of cliffside stilted buildings. By day, it showcases the exquisite charm of traditional Ba-Yu architectural aesthetics; after nightfall, illuminated by dazzling lights, it transforms into a fairy-tale “sky city”, serving as a perfect backdrop for cyberpunk-style photography and filming. A ride on the Yangtze River Cableway soars above the rushing river waters, offering panoramic views of juxtaposed old and new architecture lining both banks, allowing visitors to soak in Chongqing’s three-dimensional urban allure in mere minutes. For an immersive experience of the city’s surreal charm, a visit to Liziba Light Rail Station is essential, where visitors can witness the spectacular sight of light rail trains traversing residential buildings.
As the bustling heart of Chongqing, Jiefangbei boasts a skyline of towering high-rises evoking the vibrancy of New York’s Times Square. Adorned with shimmering neon lights day and night, it is the city’s premier hub for shopping, entertainment and cutting-edge urban experiences. To delve deep into Ba-Yu culture and the legacy of the Three Gorges Project, the Chongqing China Three Gorges Museum houses abundant and precious historical and cultural relics.
Those yearning to embrace the grandeur of the Three Gorges’ natural scenery can embark on a 4 to 5-day Yangtze River cruise covering
Qutang
,
Wu
and
Xiling
Gorges, experiencing the poetic magnificence of “a light boat glides past ten thousand lofty peaks” amid jagged peaks and emerald waters. Furthermore, two world-renowned scenic spots are not to be overlooked: the stunning landforms of Wulong Karst National Geology Park, and the Dazu Rock Carvings, a pinnacle masterpiece of ancient Chinese stone carving art.

Transportation
Chongqing serves as a vital transportation hub in southwest China, offering exceptional accessibility for travelers all over the world via direct air routes and high-speed rail networks. Nevertheless, its complex mountainous terrain renders urban transportation rather intricate. Even with navigation applications, first-time visitors can easily lose their way amid the city’s distinctive three-dimensional road system.

How to Get to Chongqing?
Chongqing Jiangbei International Airport currently operates direct international flights to 34 global destinations, including Seattle, London, Paris, Rome, Madrid, Singapore, Jakarta, Bangkok and Chiang Mai. For travelers without access to direct flights, connecting flights via major gateway cities such as Beijing and Shanghai, followed by high-speed rail or secondary air travel to Chongqing, offer a seamless alternative.
How to Get Around in Chongqing?
As a quintessential mountain city, Chongqing features an extraordinarily stereoscopic and surreal topography. A straight-line distance of merely 100 meters (110 yards) on flat digital maps often translates to arduous climbs up steep slopes, endless staircases and lengthy detours on the ground, sometimes requiring over ten minutes of walking. For this reason, flat-map straight-line distances are never a reliable reference for traveling within Chongqing.
Chongqing Metro
Chongqing Taxi
The city is equipped with a comprehensive public transportation system encompassing metro, public buses, taxis, cable cars, scenic escalators and ferries. Considering the physical exertion and time cost brought by its rugged terrain, metro and taxis are highly recommended as the preferred travel options. Cutting through mountains and spanning rivers, the metro bypasses complex ground traffic conditions efficiently, while taxis provide convenient door-to-door travel services.

Best Time to Visit
Chongqing features a subtropical humid monsoon climate with four distinct seasons. January marks its coldest month, with an average minimum temperature of 6°C (43℉), while July and August are the hottest periods, with temperatures soaring up to 40°C (104℉). Shaped by its unique terrain and climatic conditions, the city sees frequent foggy weather, with an annual average of over 100 foggy days.
Spring and autumn constitute the optimal travel seasons, boasting mild and pleasant temperatures. Despite the sweltering heat, summer features fewer foggy days, making it ideal for admiring Chongqing’s spellbinding night vistas.

Chongqing Food
Chongqing Hot Pot
Defined by bold spicy and numbing flavors, Chongqing cuisine is perfectly adapted to the city’s perennial high humidity. Local residents have long embraced the culinary wisdom of consuming chili peppers and Sichuan peppercorns to dispel bodily dampness, a time-honored lifestyle heritage passed down through generations. Chongqing hot pot and authentic Chongqing noodles are two signature delicacies not to be missed. Every bite delivers a perfect fusion of fresh ingredients and an invigorating spicy taste, creating an utterly addictive gastronomic experience.
Where to Eat in Chongqing?
What to Eat in Chongqing?
Nightlife
Chongqing’s nocturnal charm far surpasses its daytime beauty. As dusk descends, Hongya Cave and the skyscrapers of the Yuzhong Peninsula light up brilliantly, with their shimmering reflections rippling across the Yangtze and Jialing Rivers. The Two Rivers Night Cruise is a quintessential experience for first-time visitors, offering a unique perspective to appreciate the city’s dazzling riverside light displays from the water. For a tranquil riverside retreat, Nanbin Road is lined with stylish music restaurants, cozy bars and elegant teahouses, fostering a lively yet relaxing ambiance. To experience the vibrant nightlife favored by local youngsters, head to Jiujie Street, a bustling quarter packed with trendy bars, 24-hour hot pot restaurants and casual noodle stalls, integrating dining, drinking and entertainment in one vibrant destination.
Chongqing's beautiful night view
Food Street in Chonqing
Where is the Best Area to Stay in Chongqing?
Your choice of accommodation area profoundly shapes your overall travel experience in Chongqing. The Jiefangbei district stands out as the top recommendation for travelers. Located at the city’s geographic core, it is surrounded by a wealth of iconic attractions. Visitors can easily walk to Hongya Cave, the Yangtze River Cableway and Bayi Food Street. Boasting an extensive light rail network and breathtaking night views at your doorstep, it is particularly well-suited for first-time visitors. For those seeking a quieter stay with panoramic river views, Nanbin Road on the southern bank of the Yangtze River serves as an excellent alternative. Numerous riverside hotels here offer unobstructed views of the illuminated Yuzhong Peninsula nightscape.
How Long to Stay in Chongqing?
A 2 to 3-day itinerary allows for a compact yet fulfilling tour covering Chongqing’s core urban attractions. This duration is sufficient to explore iconic landmarks including Hongya Cave, Jiefangbei, the Yangtze River Cableway and Eighteen Stairs, as well as wander through local alleys to savor authentic hot pot and Chongqing noodles. Travelers wishing to take a leisurely pace and add day trips to UNESCO World Heritage Sites such as Wulong Karst National Geology Park and Dazu Rock Carvings are advised to extend their stay to 4 to 5 days. For those planning to include a Yangtze Three Gorges cruise in their itinerary, an additional 4 to 5 days will be required.

Chongqing Attractions
If one word could capture the essence of traveling in Chongqing, it would undoubtedly be “magical.” Once famed merely as a departure point for Yangtze River cruises, the city has since earned global acclaim under two iconic monikers: a cyberpunk city and an 8D magical metropolis. The dramatic interplay between its undulating terrain and layered architecture crafts a striking three-dimensional urban canvas; the riverfront glow along the Yangtze and Jialing Rivers unfolds into dreamlike, spellbinding nightscapes; and distinctive karst geology births breathtaking mountain-and-water vistas. Magic is the beating heart of Chongqing’s scenery. Unlike
Beijing
and
Xi’an
- time-honored historic capitals steeped in solemn imperial heritage - Chongqing radiates an unrestrained creativity that constantly defies conventional logic.
Hongya Cave at night
Chongqing’s modern urban fabric itself amounts to a visual odyssey. Flat thoroughfares are virtually nonexistent here; instead, bridges, tunnels and light railways weave the city’s mountains and waterways into a multi-tiered landscape. Light rail carriages glide straight through residential buildings, highways snake across rooftops, and public escalators serve as vital transit links - this is everyday life in the legendary 8D city. To soak in this unparalleled urban topography, ride the Yangtze River Cableway, gliding high above the water to gaze down upon clusters of skyscrapers lining both riverbanks; alternatively, head to Chaotianmen Dock, where the futuristic Chongqing Raffles City juts skyward like a colossal ocean liner at the confluence of the two great rivers.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
Chongqing’s historical and cultural heritage is as rich, layered and full-bodied as its signature hot pot. The cradle of millennia-old Ba-Yu civilization, it boasts over 3,000 years of recorded history and once stood as China’s wartime provisional capital during the Anti-Japanese War, leaving an indelible trail of historical relics across its land. Wandering ancient precincts such as Ciqikou and Xiahaoli, visitors will find
Ming
(1368 - 1644) and
Qing
(1644 - 1912) stilt houses lining cobblestone lanes alongside bustling specialty shops, with the warm bustle of local daily life emanating from every nook and cranny.
Geographically, Chongqing sits at the transitional zone between the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and the middle-lower Yangtze Plain, where nature unleashed its full creative prowess to craft extraordinary landscapes. Its one-of-a-kind geographic layout - cities built into mountains, mountains nested within urban sprawl, and rivers winding beneath elevated terrain - forms a naturally breathtaking masterpiece in its own right.
Top 10 Attractions to Visit
1.
Hongya Cave
Hongya Cave stands as the crown jewel of Chongqing’s night views and the most vivid embodiment of the city’s whimsical 8D charm. This 11-tier cliffside stilt-house complex rests serenely beside the Jialing River by daylight, yet transforms into a fantastical realm straight out of Spirited Away once dusk falls and its lights flicker to life. Layer upon layer of gilded illumination spills onto the river surface, shimmering in perfect harmony with the bridge spanning the river and sleek modern high-rises in the distance. Inside, an array of stalls serves iconic Chongqing snacks and local handicrafts. Here, visitors can soak in sweeping vistas, browse local wares to their heart’s content, and immerse themselves in a seamless fusion of culture, cuisine and entertainment.
Hongya Cave
Jiefangbei CBD
2.
Jiefangbei CBD
Jiefangbei functions as Chongqing’s central commercial district and an iconic spiritual landmark. At the precinct’s core rises the People’s Liberation Monument, first erected in 1940 and emblazoned with its prominent inscription. It is China’s sole monument dedicated to commemorating the nation’s victory in the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression. Ringed by glass-clad skyscrapers and luxury flagship boutiques, the district buzzes with contemporary energy by day and blazes with neon luminescence after dark, cultivating an unmistakable cyberpunk ambiance. Conveniently positioned within walking distance of nearly all major city landmarks, it serves as an indispensable starting point for first-time visitors to Chongqing.
3.
Yangtze River
Setting sail from Chaotianmen Dock, a Yangtze River cruise delivers a scenically spectacular, effortlessly tranquil journey. As vessels drift downstream, travelers witness the imposing grandeur of
Qutang Gorge
, the secluded serenity of
Wu Gorge
, and the precipitous, rugged beauty of
Xiling Gorge
unfolding in succession. Leaning against the deck railings, guests behold steep, emerald-hued mountain peaks flanking the water, wispy mist curling between summits - every instant of the voyage resembles a living Chinese landscape scroll. Life onboard unfolds at a gentle, unhurried pace: scenic sightseeing by day, lulled to rest by the river’s soft murmur after dark, offering a rare, restorative escape from the rush of modern travel.
Yangtze River
Wulong Karst
4.
Wulong Karst National Geology Park
Wulong Karst National Geology Park is hailed as nature’s sculptor’s studio, showcasing the earth’s unparalleled geological craftsmanship. Its massive sinkholes and Three Natural Bridges constitute an exceptionally rare, jaw-dropping natural wonder: sheer collapsed cliff faces, deep chasm basins and cascading waterfalls converge to craft an awe-inspiring panorama. The site featured as a filming backdrop for Transformers: Age of Extinction, and the primeval, monumental grandeur of its karst formations evokes the sensation of stepping onto the geological ruins of an alien world.
5. Light Rail Passing Through a Building‌
Liziba Light Rail Station has become the most iconic symbol of Chongqing’s surreal 8D urban topography. The mere phrase “light rail passing through a residential building” conjures an almost otherworldly, dreamlike image. Each day, throngs of tourists gather at dedicated viewing platforms, phones raised in anticipation of the iconic sight: a sleek modern train gliding slowly toward an ordinary apartment block before vanishing seamlessly into its structure. This is no contrived sci-fi spectacle, but an ingenious engineering solution forged to adapt to Chongqing’s rugged hilly terrain.
Light Rail Passing Through a Building‌
Giant panda at Chongqing Zoo
6.
Chongqing Zoo
Chongqing Zoo offers an unbeatable opportunity to encounter giant pandas. The panda enclosure is invariably the liveliest corner of the park: guests watch these beloved bears munch contentedly on bamboo, oblivious to onlookers, or tumble and frolic across wooden platforms. Their gentle, carefree demeanor effortlessly melts away travel weariness.
7. Xiahaoli Old Street
Xiahaoli Old Street, a century-old lane steeped in vintage allure and artistic flair, tops the list for immersive urban walking tours in Chongqing. Historic Western-style trading mansions stand side by side with traditional local dwellings, while winding stone staircases connect an array of artisanal boutiques and cozy cafes. As visitors amble along, the bustling Dongshuimen Bridge stretches overhead, the wide Yangtze River unfurls far below, and ancient cobblestone paths beneath lead through a dreamlike blend of bygone eras and modern life - a distinctly Chongqing experience brimming with everyday warmth, cultural depth and quiet romance.
Xiahaoli Old Street
Yangtze River Cableway View
8. Yangtze River Cableway
The Yangtze River Cableway acts as a suspended time tunnel arching over the river. Once a vital daily transit route for the city’s hillside residents, it has evolved into a quintessential aerial sightseeing ritual. As the cable car departs the station and glides across the broad river expanse, the full breadth of Chongqing unfolds beneath passengers’ feet: on one side, a dense forest of towering skyscrapers covers Yuzhong Peninsula; on the other, low-rise homes nestle amid lush greenery in the southern districts; below, golden ripples shimmer across the water as slow-moving barges drift past. This brief airborne journey distills the city’s three-dimensional topography, surreal whimsy and vibrant local vitality into a single, unforgettable experience.
9.
Chongqing China Three Gorges Museum
The Three Gorges Museum is an ideal place to gain a deep understanding of the culture of Chongqing and the Three Gorges region. With a collection of 115,000 cultural relics, it brings the area’s rich heritage to life. One of the highlights here is a large-scale model of the Three Gorges, which illustrates how the gorges were formed and showcases the region’s diverse plant and animal life. Complementing the model are remarkable exhibits such as the earliest human fossils, dating back 2.5 million years, and the largest bronze ritual vessel ever unearthed in the Chongqing area, among many other treasures.
Cultural relic at the Three Gorges Museum
Dazu Rock Carvings
10.
Dazu Rock Carvings
Where Wulong dazzles with natural magic, the Dazu Rock Carvings exude grandeur born of human artistic mastery. A UNESCO World Heritage Site anchored in Buddhist culture, they represent the pinnacle of Chinese cliff carving artistry. These sculpture groups comprise 141 existing sites, containing more than 50,000 stone statues. Distinguished by its down-to-earth, lifelike stylization, Dazu holds a unique position among China’s cave art treasures and is revered as “the crowning masterpiece in the chronicle of Chinese rock carving.” The Thousand-hand Bodhisattva, boasting 830 arms, ranks as China’s largest cliffside statue integrating sculpting, polychrome painting and gilding techniques.
